title: Classic Pancakes
summary: Fluffy buttermilk pancakes perfect for weekend mornings.
instructions: In a bowl, whisk together flour, sugar, baking powder, and salt.
In another bowl, combine milk, eggs, and melted butter.
Pour wet ingredients into dry ingredients and mix until just combined.
Heat griddle or pan over medium heat. Pour 1/4 cup batter per pancake.
Cook until bubbles form on surface, then flip and cook until golden.

title: Avocado Toast with Poached Egg
summary: Creamy avocado on sourdough topped with a perfectly poached egg.
instructions: Toast bread slices until golden brown.
Bring water to simmer in a saucepan. Add splash of vinegar.
Crack eggs into small bowls. Create whirlpool in water and gently add eggs.
Cook eggs for 3-4 minutes for runny yolks.
Mash avocado with lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Spread on toast.
Top with poached eggs and season with pepper flakes.

title: Mediterranean Quinoa Bowl
summary: Healthy quinoa bowl with fresh vegetables, feta, and lemon dressing.
instructions: Cook quinoa according to package directions. Let cool.
Dice cucumber and halve cherry tomatoes.
Thinly slice red onion and soak in cold water for 10 minutes.
Whisk together olive oil, lemon juice, salt, and pepper.
Combine quinoa, vegetables, feta, and olives in large bowl.
Toss with dressing and fresh herbs before serving.

title: Asian Chicken Lettuce Wraps
summary: Light and flavorful chicken lettuce wraps with Asian-inspired sauce.
instructions: Heat oil in large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add ground chicken and cook, breaking up, until browned.
Add garlic and ginger, cook until fragrant.
Stir in soy sauce, sesame oil, and rice vinegar.
Add water chestnuts and green onions, cook 2 minutes.
Serve chicken mixture in lettuce cups.

title: Honey Garlic Salmon
summary: Pan-seared salmon with a sweet and savory honey garlic glaze.
instructions: Pat salmon dry and season with salt and pepper.
Heat olive oil in large skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook salmon skin-side up for 4-5 minutes until golden.
Flip salmon and cook 3-4 minutes more.
Remove salmon. Add garlic, ginger to pan, cook 30 seconds.
Add honey, soy sauce, lemon juice. Simmer until thickened.
Return salmon to pan, spoon glaze over fish.

title: Beef and Broccoli Stir Fry
summary: Classic Chinese-style beef and broccoli in savory sauce.
instructions: Marinate sliced beef with 2 tbsp soy sauce and cornstarch for 15 minutes.
Blanch broccoli in boiling water for 2 minutes, then drain.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in wok over high heat.
Stir-fry beef until browned, about 3-4 minutes. Remove.
Add remaining oil, stir-fry garlic and ginger for 30 seconds.
Add broccoli, remaining soy sauce, and oyster sauce.
Return beef to wok, toss everything together. Drizzle with sesame oil.

title: Creamy Mushroom Risotto
summary: Rich and creamy arborio rice with mixed mushrooms and parmesan.
instructions: Sauté mushrooms in 2 tbsp butter until golden. Set aside.
In same pan, sauté onion until translucent.
Add garlic and rice, stir for 2 minutes until rice is toasted.
Add wine and stir until absorbed.
Add warm broth one ladle at a time, stirring constantly.
When rice is creamy and al dente, stir in mushrooms, cream, remaining butter.
Remove from heat, stir in parmesan cheese. Season and serve immediately.

title: Chicken Tikka Masala
summary: Tender chicken in a rich, creamy tomato curry sauce.
instructions: Marinate chicken with yogurt, 1 tsp garam masala, cumin for 30 minutes.
Cook chicken in batches until browned. Set aside.
Sauté onion until golden, about 8 minutes.
Add garlic, ginger, remaining spices. Cook 1 minute.
Add crushed tomatoes, simmer 15 minutes.
Stir in cream and chicken. Simmer 10 minutes.
Taste and adjust seasoning. Garnish with cilantro.

title: Fish Tacos with Lime Crema
summary: Crispy fish tacos with cabbage slaw and zesty lime crema.
instructions: Season fish with cumin, chili powder, salt, and pepper.
Make lime crema: mix sour cream, lime juice, zest, and cilantro.
Toss cabbage with lime juice and salt for slaw.
Cook fish in hot oil until flaky and golden, 3-4 minutes per side.
Warm tortillas in dry pan or microwave.
Assemble tacos: fish, slaw, avocado, and lime crema.

title: Classic Mac and Cheese
summary: Creamy, indulgent mac and cheese with a golden breadcrumb topping.
instructions: Cook pasta according to package directions. Drain and set aside.
Melt butter in large saucepan. Whisk in flour, cook 1 minute.
Gradually add milk, whisking constantly. Cook until thickened.
Remove from heat, stir in cheeses until melted.
Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg. Stir in pasta.
Transfer to baking dish, top with breadcrumbs.
Bake until bubbly and golden, about 20 minutes.

title: Buddha Bowl with Tahini Dressing
summary: Nutritious bowl with roasted vegetables, quinoa, and creamy tahini dressing.
instructions: Cook quinoa according to package directions.
Toss sweet potato and Brussels sprouts with oil, salt, and pepper.
Roast vegetables at 425°F for 20-25 minutes.
Roast chickpeas on separate pan for last 15 minutes.
Whisk tahini, lemon juice, maple syrup, and water for dressing.
Assemble bowls with quinoa, vegetables, chickpeas, and dressing.

title: Greek Chicken Bowls
summary: Mediterranean-inspired bowls with marinated chicken and fresh vegetables.
instructions: Marinate chicken with half the olive oil, lemon juice, oregano for 30 minutes.
Grill or pan-sear chicken until cooked through, 6-8 minutes per side.
Let chicken rest 5 minutes, then slice.
Make tzatziki: mix yogurt, diced cucumber, garlic, lemon juice.
Combine tomatoes, red onion, remaining olive oil and lemon.
Assemble bowls with chicken, vegetables, feta, and tzatziki.

title: Caprese Grilled Cheese
summary: Elevated grilled cheese with fresh mozzarella, basil, and tomatoes.
instructions: Butter one side of each bread slice.
Layer mozzarella, tomato, and basil on unbuttered sides.
Top with remaining bread, buttered side out.
Cook in skillet over medium heat until golden, 3-4 minutes per side.
Let cool slightly, then slice. Drizzle with balsamic glaze if using.

title: Shrimp Scampi
summary: Garlicky shrimp in white wine butter sauce over pasta.
instructions: Cook linguine according to package directions. Reserve 1 cup pasta water.
Season shrimp with salt and pepper.
Heat oil and 2 tbsp butter in large skillet over medium-high heat.
Cook shrimp until pink, about 2 minutes per side. Remove.
Add garlic to pan, cook 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add wine, lemon juice, and red pepper flakes. Simmer 2 minutes.
Toss with pasta, shrimp, remaining butter, and parsley.

title: Chocolate Chip Cookies
summary: Classic chewy chocolate chip cookies with crispy edges.
instructions: Preheat oven to 375°F. Line baking sheets with parchment.
Cream butter and both sugars until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs and vanilla until combined.
In separate bowl, whisk flour, baking soda, and salt.
Gradually mix dry ingredients into wet ingredients.
Fold in chocolate chips.
Drop rounded tablespoons onto baking sheets. Bake 9-11 minutes.

title: Overnight French Toast Casserole
summary: Make-ahead French toast casserole perfect for weekend mornings.
instructions: Grease 9x13 inch baking dish. Arrange bread cubes in dish.
Whisk eggs, milk, cream, vanilla, cinnamon, and maple syrup.
Pour egg mixture over bread. Press down gently to soak.
Cover and refrigerate overnight, at least 8 hours.
Remove from fridge 30 minutes before baking. Preheat oven to 350°F.
Drizzle with melted butter. Bake 45-50 minutes until golden.
Let rest 5 minutes. Dust with powdered sugar before serving.

title: Chicken Noodle Soup
summary: Comforting homemade chicken noodle soup with tender vegetables.
instructions: In large pot, bring broth to boil. Add chicken breasts.
Reduce heat, simmer until chicken is cooked, about 15 minutes.
Remove chicken, shred when cool. Strain and reserve broth.
In same pot, sauté onion, carrots, celery until tender.
Add garlic, cook 1 minute. Return broth to pot.
Add bay leaves, thyme, and noodles. Cook until noodles are tender.
Stir in shredded chicken. Remove bay leaves before serving.

title: Vegetarian Chili
summary: Hearty three-bean chili packed with vegetables and spices.
instructions: Heat oil in large pot. Sauté onion and peppers until soft.
Add garlic, chili powder, cumin, paprika. Cook 1 minute.
Add crushed tomatoes, all beans, and 2 cups water.
Bring to boil, then reduce heat and simmer 30 minutes.
Season with salt and pepper. Serve with toppings.

title: Pad Thai
summary: Authentic Thai stir-fried noodles with tamarind sauce and peanuts.
instructions: Soak rice noodles in warm water until soft, about 30 minutes.
Mix tamarind paste, fish sauce, and brown sugar for sauce.
Heat oil in wok over high heat. Cook shrimp until pink.
Push shrimp to one side, scramble eggs on other side.
Add drained noodles and sauce. Toss until coated.
Add bean sprouts, cook 1 minute. Garnish with peanuts and lime.

title: Margherita Pizza
summary: Classic Neapolitan pizza with fresh mozzarella, basil, and tomatoes.
instructions: Let pizza dough come to room temperature for 2 hours.
Preheat oven to 500°F with pizza stone if available.
Mix crushed tomatoes with garlic, salt, and 1 tbsp olive oil.
Stretch dough into 2 circles on floured surface.
Spread thin layer of sauce on each pizza, leaving border.
Add mozzarella pieces and drizzle with remaining olive oil.
Bake 10-12 minutes until crust is golden. Top with fresh basil.

title: Sheet-Pan Lemon Herb Chicken with Potatoes and Green Beans
summary: Crisp-skinned thighs roast right on top of the potatoes, so every bite of spud soaks up lemony, garlicky drippings.
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the potatoes on a large rimmed sheet pan with 1 tbsp olive oil and 1/2 tsp salt, then roast for 10 minutes to give them a head start.
Meanwhile, stir together the remaining 2 tbsp oil, lemon zest, half the lemon juice, garlic, oregano, thyme, 1 tsp salt and the pepper. Pat the chicken dry and rub the mixture all over it.
Push the potatoes toward the edges and nestle the chicken skin side up in the middle. Roast for 20 minutes.

Toss the green beans in the pan juices at the edges of the tray and roast 12 to 15 minutes more, until the skin is deep golden and the thickest thigh reads at least 165°F (175°F is even better for thighs).
Rest 5 minutes, drizzle with the remaining lemon juice and scatter over parsley before serving.

title: Skillet Chicken Fajitas
summary: Smoky spiced chicken and charred peppers come together in one hot pan in about half an hour, ready to pile into warm tortillas.

ingredients.name: chicken breasts
ingredients.note: boneless, skinless, sliced into thin strips

instructions: Toss the chicken strips with the chili powder, cumin, paprika, garlic powder, salt, 1 tbsp oil and half the lime juice.
Heat a large cast-iron or heavy skillet over high heat until very hot. Add the chicken in a single layer and cook 5 to 6 minutes, turning once, until browned and 165°F inside. Move to a plate.
Add the remaining 1 tbsp oil, the peppers and onion to the pan. Cook, stirring only now and then, 5 to 6 minutes until the edges char but the peppers still have some bite.
Return the chicken and any juices, squeeze in the rest of the lime and toss for 30 seconds.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet or over a gas flame for about 30 seconds per side, then fill with the fajita mix and your toppings.

title: Thai Basil Chicken (Pad Krapow Gai)
summary: A fiery, garlicky ground chicken stir-fry finished with a big handful of basil, on the table faster than takeout.

ingredients.name: thai chilies
ingredients.note: thinly sliced; use fewer for less heat

ingredients.name: thai basil
ingredients.note: leaves, loosely packed (Italian basil works too)

instructions: Cook the jasmine rice according to the package directions (about 18 minutes). Stir together the oyster sauce, soy sauce, fish sauce, brown sugar and water.
Heat the oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat. Add the garlic, shallots and chilies and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant but not browned.
Add the ground chicken and green beans if using. Cook 5 to 6 minutes, breaking the meat into small crumbles, until no pink remains and it starts to brown.
Pour in the sauce and toss for 1 minute until it coats the chicken and mostly evaporates.
Turn off the heat and fold in the basil until just wilted.
If you like, fry the eggs in hot oil until the edges are crisp and lacy. Serve the chicken over rice, topped with an egg.

title: Kung Pao Chicken
summary: Tender chicken, crunchy peanuts and blistered chilies in a glossy sweet-tangy sauce with a gentle tingle.
instructions: Toss the chicken with 1 tbsp soy sauce and 2 tsp of the cornstarch; let it sit while you prep. Whisk the remaining 2 tbsp soy sauce, remaining 1 tsp cornstarch, vinegar, sugar and water into a sauce.
Heat the oil in a wok or large skillet over medium heat. Add the dried chilies and Sichuan peppercorns and stir 30 seconds until the chilies darken slightly; don't let them blacken.
Turn the heat to high, add the chicken and spread it out. Cook 4 to 5 minutes, stirring occasionally, until browned and cooked through (165°F).
Add the garlic, ginger, bell pepper and white parts of the green onions; stir-fry 1 to 2 minutes.
Stir the sauce, pour it in and toss until it thickens and turns glossy, about 1 minute. Add the peanuts, green onion tops and sesame oil, then serve with rice.

title: Chicken Dakgalbi (Korean Spicy Chicken Stir-Fry)
summary: Gochujang-marinated chicken fried with cabbage and sweet potato until sticky and caramelized: sweet, spicy and deeply savory.

ingredients.name: chicken thighs
ingredients.note: boneless, skinless, cut into bite-size pieces

ingredients.name: gochugaru
ingredients.note: Korean chili flakes; or 1 tsp red pepper flakes

ingredients.name: sweet potato
ingredients.note: small, peeled and cut into thin half-moons

instructions: Mix the gochujang, soy sauce, gochugaru, honey, garlic, ginger and sesame oil in a bowl. Add the chicken and toss to coat.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet or wide pan over medium-high heat. Add the sweet potato and onion and cook 3 minutes, stirring.
Add the chicken with all of its marinade and spread it out. Cook 5 minutes, turning pieces occasionally, until the sauce starts to caramelize.

Add the cabbage and cook 5 to 6 minutes more, stirring often, until the cabbage is tender, the sweet potato pierces easily and the chicken is 165°F inside. Splash in 2 to 3 tbsp water if the sauce starts to catch.
Toss in the green onions for the last minute, sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve with rice or lettuce leaves.

title: Grilled Chicken Teriyaki Bowls
summary: Juicy grilled thighs brushed with a quick homemade teriyaki glaze, served over rice with steamed broccoli.
instructions: Start the rice according to the package directions. Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high (about 425°F).
Simmer the soy sauce, mirin, brown sugar, ginger and garlic in a small saucepan for 2 minutes. Stir in the cornstarch slurry and cook 30 seconds until syrupy; set aside.

Rub the chicken with the oil and grill 5 to 6 minutes per side until well marked and 165°F inside. Brush generously with teriyaki sauce during the last 2 minutes, turning once so it glazes without burning.
While the chicken cooks, steam the broccoli for 4 to 5 minutes until bright green and just tender.
Rest the chicken 3 minutes, slice, and arrange over rice with the broccoli. Spoon over the remaining sauce and finish with green onions and sesame seeds.

title: Oyakodon (Chicken and Egg Rice Bowl)
summary: Chicken and onion simmered in a sweet soy dashi, then set with softly cooked egg: gentle, cozy Japanese comfort in one pan.

ingredients.name: chicken thighs
ingredients.note: boneless, skinless, cut into bite-size pieces

instructions: Cook the rice according to the package directions (about 18 minutes).
In a medium skillet, bring the dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar to a simmer over medium heat. Add the onion and simmer 3 minutes until it softens.
Add the chicken in a single layer, cover and simmer 5 to 6 minutes, turning once, until cooked through to 165°F.
Beat the eggs just enough to break them up, leaving streaks of white. Pour two-thirds over the chicken in a circle, cover and cook 1 minute.
Pour on the rest of the egg, cover, turn off the heat and let it sit 1 minute, until the egg is just set but still glossy.
Divide the rice between bowls, slide the chicken and egg on top with some of the broth, and scatter with green onions.

title: Coconut Chicken Curry with Spinach
summary: A mellow, fragrant one-pot curry that uses up a whole bag of spinach and gets its creaminess from coconut milk.
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot or deep skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion with a pinch of salt for 6 to 7 minutes until soft and golden at the edges.
Stir in the garlic, ginger, curry powder, garam masala, turmeric and cayenne and cook 1 minute until the spices smell toasty.
Add the chicken and stir to coat in the spices, cooking 2 to 3 minutes until the outside turns opaque.

Pour in the tomatoes and coconut milk, add the salt and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook uncovered 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sauce thickens and the chicken is tender and 165°F inside.
Stir in the spinach a handful at a time until wilted, about 2 minutes. Add the lime juice, taste for salt and serve over basmati rice with cilantro.

title: Tandoori-Style Chicken Drumsticks
summary: A tangy, spice-packed yogurt marinade keeps drumsticks juicy while high oven heat chars the edges like a tandoor.
instructions: Cut two or three deep slashes into each drumstick down to the bone so the marinade can get in.

Mix the yogurt, lemon juice, garlic, ginger, garam masala, paprika, cumin, turmeric, cayenne and salt. Coat the chicken and marinate at least 30 minutes at room temperature, or up to 24 hours in the fridge.
Heat the oven to 450°F. Line a rimmed sheet pan with foil, set a rack on top if you have one and brush it with oil.
Arrange the drumsticks on the rack, leaving extra marinade clinging to them. Roast 35 to 40 minutes, turning once halfway, until charred in spots and 175°F near the bone.
For extra char, broil 2 to 3 minutes at the end, watching closely. Serve with the sliced onion, cilantro and lemon wedges.

title: Chicken Shawarma Wraps with Garlic Yogurt Sauce
summary: Warmly spiced skillet chicken, crisp veg and a punchy garlic yogurt sauce rolled up in soft pita.
instructions: Toss the chicken with 2 tbsp olive oil, half the lemon juice, the cumin, paprika, cinnamon, turmeric, two of the garlic cloves and the salt.
Stir the yogurt with the remaining garlic, remaining lemon juice and a pinch of salt to make the sauce.
Heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the chicken 5 to 6 minutes per side until well browned and 165°F inside.
Rest the chicken 3 minutes, then slice thinly and toss with any juices from the pan.
Spread each warm pita with yogurt sauce, pile on chicken, tomato, cucumber, onion and parsley, then roll up tightly and serve.

title: Cajun Chicken and Sausage Jambalaya
summary: A smoky, peppery one-pot rice dinner loaded with the holy trinity, browned chicken and andouille.
instructions: Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the sausage 4 to 5 minutes and lift it out with a slotted spoon.
Season the chicken with half the Cajun seasoning and brown it in the same pot for 5 minutes, stirring once or twice. Remove it with the sausage.
Lower the heat to medium. Add the onion, bell pepper and celery and cook 5 minutes until softened, scraping up the browned bits. Stir in the garlic, thyme and remaining Cajun seasoning for 1 minute.
Stir in the rice to coat, then add the tomatoes, broth and bay leaves. Return the chicken and sausage and bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce to low and simmer 20 to 25 minutes without stirring, until the rice is tender and has absorbed the liquid.
Remove from the heat and let it stand covered 5 minutes. Discard the bay leaves, fluff, and finish with green onions and hot sauce to taste.

title: Chicken Piccata
summary: Thin chicken cutlets in a bright lemon, caper and butter pan sauce: restaurant-worthy and done in under half an hour.

ingredients.name: chicken breasts
ingredients.note: boneless, skinless (about 1.5 lb), halved horizontally into cutlets

instructions: Pound the cutlets to an even 1/4-inch thickness. Season with salt and pepper and dredge lightly in flour, shaking off the excess.
Heat the olive oil and 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the cutlets in batches 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden and 165°F inside. Transfer to a plate.
Reduce the heat to medium, add the garlic and stir 30 seconds. Pour in the wine and broth, scraping up the browned bits, and simmer 3 to 4 minutes until reduced by about a third.
Stir in the lemon juice and capers, then swirl in the remaining 2 tbsp butter until the sauce turns silky.
Return the chicken to the pan for a minute to warm through, spooning the sauce over. Sprinkle with parsley and serve with pasta, potatoes or green beans.

title: Chicken Cacciatore with Mushrooms and Peppers
summary: Bone-in thighs braised in a rustic tomato sauce with mushrooms, peppers and herbs until they're falling-apart tender.
instructions: Pat the chicken dry and season with 1 tsp salt and the pepper. Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat and brown the thighs skin side down 6 to 7 minutes until deep golden, then flip for 2 minutes. Transfer to a plate and pour off all but 2 tbsp fat.
Add the onion, bell peppers and mushrooms with the remaining salt. Cook 7 to 8 minutes over medium heat until the mushrooms release their liquid and brown.
Stir in the garlic and pepper flakes for 30 seconds, then pour in the wine and simmer 2 minutes, scraping the bottom of the pot.
Add the crushed tomatoes, oregano and rosemary. Nestle the chicken back in skin side up, keeping the skin above the sauce.
Cover and simmer gently 25 to 30 minutes until the chicken is very tender and at least 175°F near the bone. Uncover for the last 5 minutes if the sauce needs thickening.
Discard the rosemary stem, scatter with basil and serve with polenta, crusty bread or pasta.

title: Slow Cooker Salsa Verde Chicken Tacos
summary: Three ingredients do most of the work here: chicken breasts slow-cook in tangy salsa verde until they shred at a touch.
instructions: Put the onion and garlic in the slow cooker, lay the chicken on top and sprinkle with cumin and salt. Pour the salsa verde over everything.
Cover and cook on LOW for 4 to 5 hours or HIGH for 2 1/2 to 3 hours, until the chicken reaches 165°F and shreds easily.
Shred the chicken right in the pot with two forks and stir it into the sauce. Add the lime juice and half the cilantro, then taste for salt.
Toss the cabbage with a squeeze of lime and a pinch of salt for a quick slaw.
Pile the chicken into warm tortillas with a slotted spoon and top with slaw, avocado, radishes and the rest of the cilantro. Leftovers keep 4 days in the fridge.

title: Turkey Three-Bean Chili
summary: A hearty, lean weeknight chili with plenty of beans and warm spices. It tastes even better the next day.
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the turkey and cook 6 to 7 minutes, breaking it up, until browned with no pink left.
Add the onion and bell pepper and cook 5 minutes until softened. Stir in the garlic, chili powder, cumin, paprika, oregano, salt and tomato paste and cook 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes, all three beans and the broth. Bring to a boil, then lower to a gentle simmer.
Simmer uncovered 25 to 30 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick. Add a splash of broth if it gets too dense.
Taste and adjust salt and spice, then ladle into bowls and top with avocado.

title: Turkey Zucchini Meatballs in Marinara
summary: Grated zucchini keeps these turkey meatballs incredibly moist while sneaking in a vegetable. They bake, then simmer in sauce.
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F and brush a rimmed sheet pan with the olive oil.
Wrap the grated zucchini in a clean towel and wring out as much water as you can. In a bowl, gently mix it with the turkey, breadcrumbs, parmesan, egg, garlic, Italian seasoning, salt and pepper.
Roll into 16 to 18 balls about 1 1/2 inches wide (wet hands help) and set them on the pan.
Bake 15 minutes until lightly browned.
Meanwhile, warm the marinara in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the meatballs and simmer 8 to 10 minutes, spooning sauce over them, until they reach 165°F inside.
Top with basil and extra parmesan and serve over pasta, polenta or in toasted rolls.

title: Greek Turkey Burgers with Tzatziki
summary: Herby turkey burgers with feta tucked inside stay juicy on the grill, then get a cool cucumber tzatziki on top.
instructions: Make the tzatziki: stir the yogurt, cucumber, dill, lemon juice, one garlic clove and 1/4 tsp salt. Chill until needed.
In a bowl, gently mix the turkey, feta, spinach, onion, remaining garlic, oregano and 3/4 tsp salt. Don't overwork it.
Shape into four patties about 3/4 inch thick and press a shallow dimple in the center of each so they stay flat. Brush with oil.
Heat a grill or grill pan to medium-high (about 400°F). Grill the patties 5 to 6 minutes per side until nicely charred and 165°F in the center.
Toast the buns on the grill for 30 seconds. Build the burgers with tomato slices and a generous spoonful of tzatziki.

title: Chicken Tortilla Soup
summary: A brothy, gently smoky soup built on rotisserie chicken, with crunchy tortilla strips and a squeeze of lime.
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and jalapeño 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, cumin and chili powder and stir 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and broth, bring to a boil, then simmer 10 minutes to build flavor.
Meanwhile, toss the tortilla strips with the vegetable oil and a pinch of salt. Bake at 400°F for 8 to 10 minutes, shaking once, until crisp and golden (or pan-fry them in batches).
Add the chicken, beans and corn to the soup and simmer 5 minutes until everything is hot.
Stir in the lime juice and most of the cilantro, and taste for salt. Serve topped with tortilla strips, avocado and the remaining cilantro.

title: Chicken Satay with Peanut Sauce
summary: Turmeric- and lemongrass-scented chicken skewers charred on the grill, with a rich, lightly sweet peanut dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: chicken thighs
ingredients.note: boneless, skinless, cut into long 1-inch-wide strips

ingredients.name: lemongrass
ingredients.note: tender core minced, or 1 tsp lime zest

instructions: Soak 12 wooden skewers in water for 20 minutes (skip if using metal). Mix 1/3 cup coconut milk, the fish sauce, 1 tbsp brown sugar, curry powder, turmeric, lemongrass and garlic; toss the chicken in it and marinate while you make the sauce.

For the peanut sauce, whisk the remaining 2/3 cup coconut milk, peanut butter, curry paste and 1 tsp brown sugar in a small pan over medium-low heat for 3 to 4 minutes until smooth and thickened. Stir in the lime juice and soy sauce.
Thread the chicken onto the skewers in a snake pattern and brush with oil.
Grill over medium-high heat (about 425°F) 3 to 4 minutes per side until charred at the edges and 165°F inside.
Serve hot with the peanut sauce, cucumber slices and jasmine rice.

title: Za'atar Chicken with Chickpeas and Tomatoes
summary: A one-tray dinner where za'atar-rubbed thighs roast over chickpeas that turn crisp and tomatoes that burst into a jammy sauce.

ingredients.name: chickpeas
ingredients.note: 15 oz, drained, rinsed and patted dry

ingredients.name: tahini
ingredients.note: thinned with lemon juice and water, for drizzling

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Rub the chicken with 1 1/2 tbsp olive oil, the za'atar, lemon zest, garlic and 3/4 tsp salt.
On a large rimmed sheet pan, toss the chickpeas, tomatoes and onion with the remaining oil, cumin and 1/2 tsp salt. Spread out in an even layer.
Nestle the chicken among the vegetables and add the lemon wedges.
Roast 30 to 35 minutes until the chicken is golden and 165°F inside, the tomatoes have burst and the chickpeas are crisp at the edges.
Squeeze the roasted lemon over everything, scatter with parsley and drizzle with tahini sauce if you like.

title: Instant Pot White Chicken Chili
summary: Creamy without any cream: white beans, green chiles and cumin pressure-cook with chicken into a cozy, mild chili.
instructions: Set the Instant Pot to Sauté. Heat the oil and cook the onion and jalapeño 4 minutes, then add the garlic, cumin, oregano and salt and stir 1 minute.
Add the green chiles, one can of the beans, the broth and the chicken breasts. Scrape the bottom to loosen any browned bits so you don't get a burn warning.
Lock the lid and pressure cook on High for 12 minutes, then let the pressure release naturally for 10 minutes before venting the rest.
Lift out the chicken and shred it. Mash the second can of beans with a fork and stir it in with the corn, cream cheese and shredded chicken.
Switch to Sauté and simmer 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until the cream cheese melts and the chili thickens. Add the lime juice, taste for salt and top with cilantro.

title: Greek Lemon Chicken Orzo Soup
summary: A silky avgolemono-style soup where tempered egg and lemon turn plain broth into something velvety and bright.
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion, carrots and celery 6 minutes until softened, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the broth and bring to a boil. Stir in the orzo and simmer 8 to 9 minutes until tender.
Add the chicken and spinach and simmer 2 minutes until heated through. Reduce the heat to the lowest setting so the soup is no longer bubbling.
Whisk the eggs and lemon juice in a bowl until frothy. Slowly whisk in 2 ladles of hot broth, one at a time, to warm the eggs gently.
Pour the egg mixture back into the pot while stirring constantly. Heat 2 minutes, without letting it boil, until the soup turns slightly thick and creamy.
Season with salt and pepper, stir in the dill and serve right away.

title: Blackened Chicken Salad with Corn and Avocado
summary: Spicy, crusty seared chicken on a crunchy salad with sweet corn, tomatoes and avocado, all tied together by a zippy lime dressing.

ingredients.name: corn
ingredients.note: fresh, frozen and thawed, or canned

instructions: Mix the paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, thyme, cayenne and salt. Rub 1 tbsp olive oil over the chicken, then coat it evenly with the spice mix.
Heat a cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat with 1 tbsp oil. Sear the chicken 5 to 6 minutes per side, without moving it, until a dark crust forms and it reads 165°F inside. Rest 5 minutes.
In the hot skillet, char the corn for 2 to 3 minutes, stirring once or twice, then let it cool slightly.
Whisk the lime juice, honey, remaining 3 tbsp olive oil and a pinch of salt.
Toss the romaine, corn, tomatoes and onion with most of the dressing. Top with avocado and sliced chicken and drizzle over the rest.

title: Turkey and Black Bean Stuffed Peppers
summary: Sweet bell pepper halves filled with a cumin-spiced turkey, bean and rice mixture and baked under melted cheese.
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Set the pepper halves cut side up in a baking dish, add 1/4 cup water to the dish, cover with foil and bake 10 minutes to soften.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the turkey and onion 7 to 8 minutes, breaking up the meat, until browned and no pink remains.
Stir in the garlic, chili powder, cumin and salt for 1 minute, then fold in the beans, rice and salsa and heat through.
Pack the filling into the pepper halves and sprinkle with the cheese.
Bake uncovered 20 to 25 minutes until the peppers are tender and the cheese is bubbling and browned in spots. Top with cilantro.

title: Filipino Chicken Adobo
summary: Chicken braised in vinegar, soy, garlic and bay until tangy and deeply savory, then reduced to a glossy sauce for spooning over rice.
instructions: Heat the oil in a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken skin side down for 6 to 7 minutes until golden, then flip for 1 minute and pour off all but 1 tbsp fat.
Add the garlic and cook 1 minute until fragrant. Pour in the vinegar and let it bubble for 2 minutes without stirring to mellow its sharpness.
Add the soy sauce, water, bay leaves, peppercorns and brown sugar. Bring to a boil, cover and simmer on low for 25 minutes, turning the chicken once.
Uncover, raise the heat to medium and simmer 8 to 10 minutes more, spooning sauce over the chicken, until the sauce reduces by about half and the chicken is at least 175°F near the bone.
Discard the bay leaves, scatter with green onions and serve with steamed rice and plenty of sauce.

title: Buffalo Chicken Wraps
summary: Rotisserie chicken tossed in tangy buffalo sauce and rolled up with crisp lettuce, celery and ranch: lunch in 15 minutes.
instructions: Whisk the hot sauce and melted butter in a bowl.
Warm the chicken in a skillet over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes (or in the microwave), then toss it with the buffalo sauce.
Warm the tortillas for 20 seconds each in a dry skillet so they fold without cracking.
Spread each tortilla with ranch, then layer on lettuce, celery, carrot, buffalo chicken and blue cheese if using.
Fold in the sides, roll up tightly, and cut in half on the diagonal. Serve right away, or wrap in foil for a packed lunch.

title: Slow Cooker Moroccan Chicken with Sweet Potatoes
summary: Warm spices, sweet potatoes and apricots slow-cook with chicken thighs into a fragrant, gently sweet stew.

ingredients.name: sweet potatoes
ingredients.note: medium, peeled and cut into 1-inch chunks

instructions: Scatter the sweet potatoes, carrots and onion over the bottom of a 6-quart slow cooker.
Mix the garlic, ginger, cumin, cinnamon, paprika, turmeric and salt, rub it over the chicken and lay the thighs on the vegetables.
Pour in the tomatoes and broth and scatter the apricots on top.
Cover and cook on LOW for 6 hours or HIGH for 3 1/2 hours, until the chicken is tender and 165°F inside and the sweet potatoes are soft.
Break the chicken into large chunks, stir in the lemon juice, and taste for salt. Serve over couscous or rice, topped with cilantro.

title: Chicken and Broccoli Stir-Fry with Ginger Garlic Sauce
summary: Velvety chicken and crisp-tender broccoli in a savory ginger-garlic sauce, faster than waiting for delivery.

ingredients.name: broccoli
ingredients.note: about 1 lb, cut into small florets

instructions: Toss the chicken with 2 tsp cornstarch and 1 tbsp soy sauce. In a small bowl, whisk the remaining 2 tbsp soy sauce, remaining 1 tsp cornstarch, oyster sauce, broth and brown sugar.

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat. Add the chicken in one layer and cook 2 minutes without moving, then stir-fry 2 minutes more until cooked through (165°F). Transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and the broccoli with 3 tbsp water. Cover and cook 3 minutes, until bright green and crisp-tender.
Uncover, add the garlic, ginger and pepper flakes and stir-fry 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return the chicken, stir the sauce and pour it in. Toss 1 minute until glossy and thickened, then drizzle with sesame oil and serve over rice.

title: Beef Picadillo with Potatoes
summary: A savory-sweet Latin skillet of ground beef, diced potato, tomatoes, olives and raisins that comes together in one pan.
instructions: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the onion and bell pepper and cook 4 minutes until softened.
Add the ground beef and garlic. Cook, breaking the meat apart, until no pink remains, about 5 minutes. Spoon off excess fat.
Stir in the potato cubes, cumin and oregano and cook 1 minute.

Add the tomato sauce, water, olives and raisins. Season with salt and pepper, bring to a simmer, then cover and cook over medium-low 12 to 15 minutes until a potato cube is easily pierced with a fork.
Uncover and simmer 2 more minutes if the sauce looks thin. Taste, adjust seasoning and serve over rice.

title: Weeknight Ground Beef Tacos
summary: Homemade spice mix and a splash of tomato give these tacos a saucy, well-seasoned filling that beats any packet.
instructions: Brown the ground beef and onion in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking up the meat, until no pink remains, 6 to 7 minutes. Drain off most of the fat.
Add the garlic, chili powder, cumin, paprika and oregano and stir for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Stir in the tomato paste, water and salt. Simmer 4 to 5 minutes until the liquid reduces to a glossy sauce that clings to the meat.
Meanwhile, warm the tortillas in a dry skillet 30 seconds per side, or wrapped in a damp towel in the microwave for 45 seconds.
Fill each tortilla with beef and top with lettuce, tomato, cheddar and cilantro. Serve with lime wedges.

title: Classic Beef and Bean Chili
summary: A thick, deeply spiced pot of chili that tastes even better the next day and freezes beautifully.
instructions: Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the beef and cook, breaking it up, until browned, 8 minutes. Spoon off all but about 1 tablespoon of fat.
Add the onion, bell peppers and jalapeno and cook 5 minutes until soft. Stir in the garlic, chili powder, cumin, paprika, oregano and tomato paste and cook 1 minute.
Add the crushed tomatoes, beans, broth and salt. Bring to a boil, then reduce to a low simmer.
Cook partially covered for 45 minutes, stirring every 10 minutes, until thick and the flavors have melded. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick.
Taste and adjust salt and heat. Serve topped with green onions and avocado.

title: Italian Meatballs in Marinara
summary: Tender beef-and-pork meatballs baked until browned, then simmered in marinara so they soak up the sauce.

ingredients.name: Parmesan Cheese
ingredients.note: finely grated, plus more for serving

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F and line a rimmed baking sheet with foil or parchment.
In a large bowl, stir the breadcrumbs and milk together and let sit 5 minutes to soften.
Add the beef, pork, egg, parmesan, garlic, parsley, Italian seasoning, salt and pepper. Mix gently with your hands until just combined; overmixing makes them tough.
Roll into about 20 meatballs, 1 1/2 inches wide, and space them on the sheet. Bake 15 minutes until browned.
Warm the marinara in a wide pot over medium heat. Add the meatballs and simmer gently, covered, 15 minutes until the centers reach 160°F.
Serve over spaghetti or in rolls, with extra parmesan.

title: Mushroom Swiss Burgers
summary: Juicy skillet burgers smothered in garlicky browned mushrooms and melted Swiss, a great use for mushrooms about to turn.
instructions: Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms in a single layer and cook without stirring 3 minutes, then stir and cook 3 more until browned.
Stir in the garlic, Worcestershire and a pinch of salt for 30 seconds. Transfer to a bowl and wipe out the pan.
Divide the beef into 4 portions and shape into patties 1/2 inch wider than the buns, pressing a shallow dimple in each center. Season both sides with the salt and pepper.
Heat the remaining butter in the skillet over medium-high. Cook the patties 4 minutes, flip, and cook 3 to 4 minutes more until they reach 160°F.
Pile mushrooms on each patty, top with a slice of Swiss, cover the pan and cook 1 minute until the cheese melts.
Spread buns with mayonnaise, add lettuce and the burgers, and serve.

title: Pork Chops with Apples and Onions
summary: Golden seared chops finished in a buttery pan sauce of soft apples, onion and thyme. Fall comfort in 30 minutes.
instructions: Pat the chops dry and season with salt and pepper. Let sit while you slice the onion and apples.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Sear the chops 4 minutes per side until well browned and 140°F inside; move to a plate.
Reduce heat to medium, add the butter, onion and thyme, and cook 4 minutes until the onion softens.
Add the apples and brown sugar and cook 4 minutes, stirring, until the apples are tender at the edges.
Pour in the broth and vinegar, scraping up the browned bits. Return the chops and any juices, cover and simmer 2 to 3 minutes until the pork reaches 145°F.
Rest the chops 3 minutes, then serve with apples, onions and pan sauce spooned over.

title: Garlic Herb Pork Tenderloin and Potatoes
summary: A lean pork tenderloin roasted on one sheet pan with crispy potatoes and green beans, all under 45 minutes.
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the potatoes with 1 tablespoon oil and 1/2 teaspoon salt on a rimmed sheet pan and roast 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, stir together the remaining oil, garlic, rosemary, thyme, mustard, 1 teaspoon salt and pepper. Rub two-thirds over the pork; toss the green beans with the rest.
Push the potatoes to the edges, lay the tenderloin in the center and scatter the green beans around it.
Roast 18 to 22 minutes, until a thermometer in the thickest part of the pork reads 145°F and the potatoes are golden.
Rest the pork on a board for 5 minutes, then slice 1/2 inch thick. Serve with the vegetables and lemon wedges.

title: Slow Cooker Pork Carnitas
summary: Citrus-braised pork shoulder that shreds with a fork, then gets crisped under the broiler for those irresistible edges.

ingredients.name: Pork Shoulder
ingredients.note: boneless, cut into 3-inch chunks, excess fat trimmed

instructions: Mix the salt, cumin, oregano and chili powder and rub all over the pork chunks.
Put the onion, garlic and bay leaves in the slow cooker, add the pork, then pour the orange and lime juice over and tuck in the squeezed orange halves.
Cover and cook on LOW 8 hours (or HIGH 5 hours) until the pork shreds easily with a fork.
Discard the orange halves, onion and bay leaves. Shred the pork with two forks and toss with about 1/2 cup of the cooking juices.
Heat the broiler with a rack 6 inches from the element. Spread the pork on a rimmed sheet pan and broil 5 to 8 minutes until the edges are crisp, stirring once.
Serve in warm tortillas with cilantro and diced onion. Refrigerate leftovers in their juices up to 4 days.

title: Skillet Sausage, Peppers and Zucchini
summary: Browned Italian sausage with sweet peppers, onions and zucchini in one skillet. A great clean-out-the-crisper dinner.
instructions: Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Brown the sausages on all sides, about 6 minutes; move to a board and slice into 1-inch pieces (they will finish cooking later).
Add the peppers and onion to the fat in the pan and cook 6 minutes, stirring now and then, until softened with some browned edges.
Add the zucchini, garlic, Italian seasoning and pepper flakes and cook 3 minutes.
Return the sausage, stir in the crushed tomatoes, cover and simmer 8 to 10 minutes until the sausage reaches 160°F and the zucchini is just tender.
Season with salt, scatter basil over and serve on its own, over polenta, or in toasted rolls.

title: Lamb Kofta with Cucumber Yogurt Sauce
summary: Warmly spiced lamb skewers with onion and herbs, grilled or broiled and served with a cool, garlicky yogurt sauce.
instructions: If using wooden skewers, soak 8 of them in water for 15 minutes.
In a bowl, combine the lamb, onion, two-thirds of the garlic, parsley, half the mint, cumin, coriander, cinnamon, salt and pepper. Mix with your hands for 1 minute until slightly sticky.
Divide into 8 portions and press each around a skewer into a 5-inch log. Chill 10 minutes if they feel soft.
Stir the yogurt, cucumber, lemon juice, remaining garlic and mint with a pinch of salt; refrigerate until serving.
Grill over medium-high heat (or broil 4 inches from the element) 8 to 10 minutes, turning every 2 minutes, until browned and 160°F inside.
Serve with the yogurt sauce and a chopped tomato-cucumber salad, plus rice or gluten-free flatbread if you like.

title: Vietnamese Lemongrass Pork Noodle Bowls
summary: Caramelized lemongrass pork over cool rice noodles, crisp vegetables and herbs, dressed with a bright lime-fish sauce dressing.
instructions: Make the dressing: stir 3 tablespoons fish sauce, 2 tablespoons brown sugar, the lime juice, warm water and one-quarter of the garlic until the sugar dissolves.
Cook the rice noodles according to the package (usually 3 to 5 minutes in boiling water), drain, rinse under cold water and drain well.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high. Add the lemongrass, shallot and remaining garlic and stir 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the pork, 1 tablespoon fish sauce and 1 tablespoon brown sugar. Cook, breaking it up, 6 to 8 minutes until cooked through and browned and caramelized in spots.
Divide noodles among bowls and top with lettuce, cucumber, carrot, pork, mint and cilantro.
Spoon the dressing over each bowl and finish with peanuts and jalapeno.

title: Filipino Pork Adobo
summary: Pork braised in soy, vinegar, garlic and bay until tender, then reduced to a glossy, tangy sauce made for spooning over rice.
instructions: Combine the pork, soy sauce, vinegar, water, garlic, bay leaves and peppercorns in a heavy pot. Bring to a boil over medium-high without stirring, which lets the vinegar's sharpness mellow.
Reduce heat to low, cover and simmer 50 to 60 minutes until the pork is fork-tender.
Lift the pork out with a slotted spoon. Stir the brown sugar into the liquid and boil it 8 to 10 minutes until reduced by about half.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high and brown the pork pieces 4 to 5 minutes, turning, until crisp on the edges.
Return the pork to the sauce and toss to coat. Discard the bay leaves, sprinkle with green onions and serve over rice.

title: Sichuan-Style Pork and Green Beans
summary: Blistered green beans tossed with savory ground pork, garlic and chili in a quick wok stir-fry that's big on flavor.
instructions: Stir together the soy sauce, rice vinegar and sugar in a small bowl.
Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat. Add the green beans and cook, tossing every minute, 6 to 7 minutes until blistered and wrinkled in spots. Transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and the pork. Cook, breaking it up, 4 minutes until browned and a little crisp.
Add the garlic, ginger and pepper flakes and stir 30 seconds until fragrant.
Return the beans, pour in the sauce and toss 1 minute until glossy. Turn off the heat, drizzle with sesame oil and toss in the green onions. Serve over rice.

title: Bacon Fried Cabbage
summary: Smoky bacon and sweet, lightly charred cabbage turn a humble head of cabbage into a hearty skillet supper or side.
instructions: Cook the bacon in a large, deep skillet over medium heat 7 to 8 minutes until crisp. Scoop it out with a slotted spoon, leaving the fat in the pan.
Raise the heat to medium-high, add the onion and cook 3 minutes until starting to soften.
Add the cabbage in batches, letting each handful wilt before adding more. Cook 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally and letting it sit between stirs so it browns in spots.
Stir in the garlic, paprika and pepper flakes for 30 seconds, then add the vinegar and scrape up any browned bits.
Return the bacon, season with salt and pepper and serve hot.

title: Beer-Braised Bratwurst with Sauerkraut
summary: Bratwurst browned then simmered with beer, onions and sauerkraut for a cozy German-style dinner with plenty of mustard.
instructions: Heat the oil in a large, deep skillet over medium heat. Brown the bratwurst on all sides, about 6 minutes, then move to a plate.
Add the onions and cook 8 to 10 minutes, stirring often, until soft and golden.
Pour in the beer and scrape up the browned bits. Stir in the sauerkraut, brown sugar and caraway.
Nestle the brats into the pan, bring to a simmer, cover and cook over medium-low 15 minutes until the sausages reach 160°F.
Uncover and simmer 5 more minutes to reduce the liquid slightly. Serve the brats over the sauerkraut and onions with mustard and boiled potatoes.

title: Beef Stroganoff
summary: Quick-seared strips of sirloin in a silky mushroom and sour cream sauce, served over buttery egg noodles.

ingredients.name: Sirloin Steak
ingredients.note: sliced against the grain into thin strips

instructions: Start a pot of salted water for the noodles; cook them according to the package while you make the sauce.

Pat the beef dry and season with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large skillet over high heat and sear the beef in two batches, 1 to 2 minutes per batch, until browned but still pink inside. Transfer to a plate.
Reduce heat to medium and add the butter, mushrooms and onion. Cook 6 to 7 minutes until the mushrooms are browned and their liquid has evaporated.
Stir in the garlic and flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the broth and mustard. Simmer 3 minutes until thickened.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the sour cream until smooth, then return the beef and its juices. Warm over low 1 to 2 minutes without boiling so the sauce doesn't split.
Serve over the drained noodles, sprinkled with parsley.

title: Slow Cooker Pot Roast with Vegetables
summary: Fall-apart chuck roast slowly braised with carrots, potatoes and herbs, with the juices turned into an easy gravy.
instructions: Pat the roast dry and season all over with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high and sear 4 to 5 minutes per side until deeply browned.
Put the onion, carrots, potatoes and garlic in the slow cooker and set the roast on top.
Stir the tomato paste into the hot skillet for 30 seconds, then add the broth and scrape up the browned bits. Pour over the roast and tuck in the thyme, rosemary and bay leaves.
Cover and cook on LOW 8 hours (or HIGH 5 hours) until the beef shreds easily with a fork.

Move the beef and vegetables to a platter. Discard the herbs and skim fat from the liquid. Pour the liquid into a saucepan, bring to a boil, whisk in the cornstarch mixed with cold water and simmer 1 minute until thickened.
Break the beef into chunks and serve with the vegetables and gravy.

title: Beef Bulgogi
summary: Thin-sliced beef in a sweet soy, pear and sesame marinade, seared hot so the edges caramelize in minutes.
instructions: Whisk the soy sauce, grated pear, brown sugar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger and pepper in a bowl.
Add the beef, onion and green onions and toss to coat. Marinate at least 15 minutes at room temperature, or up to 8 hours refrigerated.
Heat a large skillet or cast-iron pan over high heat until very hot and add the oil.
Lift the beef out of the marinade and cook in 2 or 3 batches, spreading it in a single layer. Sear 1 to 2 minutes per side until browned at the edges and just cooked through.
Serve over rice sprinkled with sesame seeds, with kimchi or lettuce leaves for wrapping if you like.

title: Cumin Lamb Stir-Fry
summary: A punchy Xi'an-inspired stir-fry of lamb with toasted cumin, chili and onions, finished with a big handful of cilantro.
instructions: Toss the lamb with 1/2 tablespoon soy sauce and the cornstarch and let sit 10 minutes.

Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat until shimmering. Spread the lamb in a single layer and sear 1 minute without moving, then stir-fry 1 minute more until browned. Remove to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and the onion and jalapeno. Stir-fry 2 minutes until the onion is crisp-tender.
Add the cumin, pepper flakes and garlic and stir 30 seconds until very fragrant.
Return the lamb with the remaining soy sauce, salt and sugar and toss 1 minute. Turn off the heat, toss in the cilantro and serve over rice.

title: Sloppy Joes
summary: Tangy, slightly sweet ground beef with peppers and onions piled onto toasted buns. A fast family favorite.
instructions: Cook the beef, onion and bell pepper in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking up the meat, 7 to 8 minutes until the beef is browned and the vegetables soft. Drain excess fat.
Stir in the garlic and chili powder for 30 seconds.
Add the tomato sauce, ketchup, brown sugar, Worcestershire, mustard and salt.
Simmer over medium-low 10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until thick enough to mound on a spoon.
Spoon onto toasted buns and serve with pickles or coleslaw.

title: Pork Tonkatsu with Cabbage Slaw
summary: Crisp panko-crusted pork cutlets with a quick homemade tonkatsu sauce and a pile of fresh shredded cabbage.
instructions: Stir the ketchup, Worcestershire, soy sauce and sugar together for the sauce. Toss the cabbage with the rice vinegar and a pinch of salt and keep cold.
Make a few small cuts through the fat along the edge of each chop so they stay flat. Pound to an even 1/2 inch and season with salt and pepper.
Set out three shallow dishes with flour, beaten eggs and panko. Dredge each chop in flour, dip in egg, then press firmly into the panko.
Heat the oil in a large heavy skillet over medium-high to 350°F (a panko crumb should sizzle immediately).
Fry 2 cutlets at a time, 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deep golden and the pork reaches 145°F. Drain on a rack and let rest 2 minutes.
Slice into strips and serve with the cabbage, sauce and lemon wedges.

title: Beef and Rice Stuffed Peppers
summary: Bell peppers filled with seasoned beef, rice and tomato, baked under a blanket of melted cheese.

ingredients.name: Bell Peppers
ingredients.note: large, tops cut off and seeded

instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F. Stand the peppers in a baking dish just big enough to hold them upright.
Brown the beef and onion in a skillet over medium-high heat 7 minutes, breaking up the meat; drain the fat. Stir in the garlic, Italian seasoning, paprika, salt and pepper for 30 seconds.
Off the heat, stir in the rice, drained tomatoes and half the tomato sauce.
Pack the filling into the peppers. Mix the remaining tomato sauce with the reserved tomato juice and pour it into the bottom of the dish.
Cover with foil and bake 30 minutes. Uncover, top with the mozzarella and bake 12 to 15 minutes more until the peppers are tender and the cheese is bubbly.
Let rest 5 minutes, sprinkle with parsley and serve.

title: Thai Pork Larb
summary: A zesty warm salad of minced pork with lime, fish sauce, chili and lots of fresh herbs, eaten in crisp lettuce cups.
instructions: Toast the raw rice in a dry skillet over medium heat, shaking the pan, 5 minutes until deep golden. Cool briefly, then grind to a coarse powder in a spice grinder or mortar.
In the same skillet over medium heat, add the pork and water. Cook, breaking it into fine crumbles, 5 to 6 minutes until no pink remains. Turn off the heat.
Stir in the fish sauce, lime juice, sugar and pepper flakes, then fold in the shallots.
Add the toasted rice powder, green onions, mint and cilantro and toss. Taste; it should be sour, salty and spicy, so adjust with more lime or fish sauce.
Serve warm or at room temperature spooned into lettuce leaves, with cucumber slices on the side.

title: Flank Steak with Chimichurri
summary: Quick-seared flank steak sliced thin and topped with a bright, garlicky parsley and oregano sauce.
instructions: Pat the steak dry and season with 1 teaspoon salt and the pepper. Let it sit at room temperature while you make the sauce.
For the chimichurri, stir together the parsley, oregano, garlic, vinegar, pepper flakes and remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt, then stir in the olive oil. Let stand at least 10 minutes.
Heat a grill to high or a cast-iron skillet over high heat with the vegetable oil until just smoking.
Cook the steak 4 to 6 minutes per side, until it reaches 130°F in the thickest part for medium-rare.
Rest the steak on a board for 5 minutes, then slice thinly against the grain.
Spoon chimichurri over the slices and serve the rest on the side.

title: Miso-Glazed Salmon with Quick Cucumber Salad
summary: Salmon broiled under a sweet-salty miso glaze until lacquered, served with a crisp rice-vinegar cucumber salad.
instructions: Heat the broiler with a rack about 6 inches below it and line a sheet pan with foil. Pat the salmon dry and set it skin-side down on the pan.
Whisk the miso, honey, soy sauce, 1 tbsp of the rice vinegar, sesame oil and ginger into a smooth glaze.
Toss the cucumber with the remaining 1 tbsp rice vinegar, the sugar and a pinch of salt; set aside while the fish cooks.
Spread most of the glaze over the tops of the fillets. Broil 6 to 8 minutes, brushing on the rest of the glaze halfway, until the top is deeply browned in spots.
Check doneness: the thickest part should flake easily and read 145°F. If the glaze darkens before the center is cooked, cover loosely with foil and broil 1 to 2 minutes more.
Serve the salmon over rice if you like, topped with green onion and sesame seeds, with the drained cucumbers on the side.

title: Sheet-Pan Salmon with Zucchini and Cherry Tomatoes
summary: One pan, one bake: lemony salmon roasts alongside zucchini and blistered cherry tomatoes that turn into their own sauce.

ingredients.name: Zucchini
ingredients.note: halved lengthwise and sliced 1/2 inch thick

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Line a large rimmed sheet pan with parchment.
Toss the zucchini, cherry tomatoes and onion with 2 tbsp olive oil, half the garlic, the oregano, salt and pepper. Spread on the pan and roast 8 minutes.
Meanwhile, pat the salmon dry and rub with the remaining 1 tbsp oil, the rest of the garlic, the lemon zest, salt and pepper.
Push the vegetables to the edges, nestle the salmon in the center and scatter the olives around. Roast 10 to 12 minutes, until the salmon flakes easily and reaches 145°F and the tomatoes have burst.
Squeeze a couple of lemon wedges over everything, stir the tomato juices into the vegetables and finish with parsley. Serve with the remaining wedges.

title: Blackened Salmon with Avocado Salsa
summary: A smoky homemade Cajun spice crust seared hard in a hot skillet, cooled down with a chunky avocado and tomato salsa.
instructions: Stir the paprika, garlic powder, onion powder, thyme, cayenne and salt together. Pat the salmon very dry and press the spice mix onto all sides.
Gently fold the avocado, tomato, red onion, lime juice, cilantro and a pinch of salt together in a bowl. Set aside.
Heat a large cast-iron or heavy skillet over medium-high heat until very hot, then add the oil. Open a window or turn on the fan; blackening is smoky.
Lay in the salmon, presentation side down, and cook without moving for 3 to 4 minutes until a dark crust forms.
Flip and cook 3 to 4 minutes more, until the fish flakes at the thickest point and reads 145°F.
Spoon the avocado salsa over the salmon and serve right away.

title: Salmon Poke Bowls
summary: Cubes of sushi-grade salmon tossed in a gingery tamari dressing over rice, with cucumber, avocado and crunchy toppings.

ingredients.name: Salmon
ingredients.note: sushi-grade, skin removed, cut into 3/4-inch cubes

ingredients.name: Cooked White Rice
ingredients.note: sushi or short-grain, warm or room temperature

ingredients.name: Sriracha
ingredients.note: stirred into a little mayonnaise if you like

instructions: Buy salmon labeled sushi- or sashimi-grade and keep it cold until the moment you use it.
Whisk the tamari, sesame oil, rice vinegar, honey and ginger in a medium bowl.
Add the cubed salmon and most of the green onion and toss gently to coat. Chill 10 minutes while you prep the vegetables (no longer than an hour).
Divide the rice among 4 bowls and arrange the cucumber, avocado and carrot on top.
Spoon the salmon and any dressing over the bowls, then finish with sesame seeds, the remaining green onion and a drizzle of sriracha if you want heat.

title: Canned Salmon Cakes with Lemon-Dill Sauce
summary: A budget pantry dinner: canned salmon, panko and herbs pan-fried into golden cakes with a bright yogurt dipping sauce.

ingredients.name: Canned Salmon
ingredients.note: drained, large bones and skin removed

instructions: Flake the salmon into a bowl. Add the egg, panko, mayonnaise, mustard, green onion, lemon zest, 1 tbsp of the dill and a few grinds of pepper. Mix until it holds together.
Shape into 8 patties about 1/2 inch thick. If they feel loose, chill 10 minutes to firm up.
Stir the yogurt with the remaining dill, 1 tbsp lemon juice and a pinch of salt for the sauce.
Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Cook the cakes 3 to 4 minutes per side, until deep golden and hot through (160°F in the center because of the egg).
Serve the cakes over greens with the lemon-dill sauce and extra lemon juice squeezed over.

title: Thai Red Curry Shrimp
summary: Plump shrimp simmered in coconut red curry with bell pepper and spinach, ready in about 25 minutes.

ingredients.name: Basil
ingredients.note: Thai basil if you can find it

instructions: Heat the oil in a large skillet or wide pot over medium heat. Cook the shallot and garlic 2 minutes until soft.
Add the curry paste and stir constantly for 1 minute, until fragrant and darkened slightly.
Spoon in the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk and fry it with the paste for 1 minute, then pour in the rest of the can, the fish sauce and the brown sugar. Bring to a simmer.
Add the bell pepper and simmer 4 minutes, until crisp-tender.
Add the shrimp and cook 3 to 4 minutes, stirring once, just until they curl and turn pink and opaque.
Turn off the heat and stir in the spinach, lime juice and basil until the greens wilt. Taste and adjust with more fish sauce or lime, then serve over rice.

title: Gambas al Ajillo
summary: Spanish tapas-bar garlic shrimp sizzled in olive oil with chili and smoked paprika; easily scaled into a dinner.

ingredients.name: Shrimp
ingredients.note: large, peeled and deveined, tails on or off

instructions: Pat the shrimp dry and toss with the salt.
Put the olive oil and garlic in a large skillet and set over medium-low heat. Cook 3 to 4 minutes, until the garlic is fragrant and just turning pale gold; do not let it brown.
Add the red pepper flakes and paprika, then raise the heat to medium-high and add the shrimp in a single layer.
Cook about 2 minutes, flip, and cook 1 to 2 minutes more until the shrimp are pink and opaque all the way through.
Splash in the sherry if using and let it bubble 30 seconds. Take off the heat and stir in the lemon juice and parsley.
Serve straight from the pan with rice or crusty bread (skip the bread to keep it gluten-free) to soak up the garlic oil.

title: Cajun Shrimp and Cheddar Grits
summary: Creamy cheddar grits topped with spicy shrimp in a quick pan sauce of peppers, onion, garlic and lemon.
instructions: Bring the water, milk and 1/2 tsp salt to a simmer in a saucepan. Slowly whisk in the grits, lower the heat and cook, stirring often, 20 to 25 minutes until thick and tender (add a splash of water if too stiff).
While the grits cook, toss the shrimp with the Cajun seasoning.
Melt 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the shrimp and sear 1 to 2 minutes per side until just pink and opaque. Transfer to a plate.

Add another 1 tbsp butter, the bell pepper and onion to the skillet and cook 4 minutes until soft. Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then pour in the broth and scrape up the browned bits. Simmer 2 minutes.
Return the shrimp and juices to the pan, add the lemon juice and hot sauce, and toss to warm through.
Stir the cheddar and remaining 1 tbsp butter into the grits and season with salt. Spoon into bowls, top with the shrimp and sauce, and scatter with green onion.

title: Gochujang Shrimp Rice Bowls
summary: Sticky, sweet-hot gochujang shrimp over rice with quick-pickled cucumber and shredded cabbage.
instructions: Toss the cucumber with 2 tbsp rice vinegar, the sugar and a pinch of salt. Set aside to quick-pickle.
Whisk the gochujang, soy sauce, honey, the remaining 1 tbsp rice vinegar, sesame oil and garlic into a sauce.
Pat the shrimp dry. Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the shrimp in one layer, about 2 minutes per side, until pink and opaque.
Lower the heat to medium, pour in the sauce and toss for 30 to 60 seconds until it bubbles and clings to the shrimp. Don't let it scorch.
Divide the rice among bowls, top with cabbage, the drained cucumbers and the shrimp, then finish with green onion and sesame seeds.

title: Shrimp Tacos with Cabbage-Lime Slaw
summary: Chili-rubbed shrimp seared in minutes and piled into warm corn tortillas with a crunchy lime-cilantro slaw.
instructions: Toss the cabbage with the cilantro, juice of 1 lime, the mayonnaise and a good pinch of salt. Let it sit while you cook so it softens slightly.
Pat the shrimp dry and toss with the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder and 1/2 tsp salt.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the shrimp in one layer 1 1/2 to 2 minutes per side, until pink and opaque. Squeeze the remaining lime over them.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet or directly over a gas flame for about 30 seconds per side, then wrap in a towel to keep soft.
Fill each tortilla with slaw and shrimp, then top with avocado and jalapeno. Serve with lime wedges.

title: Tuscan White Bean and Tuna Salad
summary: A no-cook pantry lunch of good canned tuna, creamy white beans, cherry tomatoes and arugula in a lemony dressing.
instructions: Soak the sliced red onion in cold water for 5 minutes to soften its bite, then drain.
Whisk the lemon zest, lemon juice, olive oil, mustard, 1/2 tsp salt and plenty of pepper in a large bowl.
Add the beans, cherry tomatoes, onion, celery and parsley and toss to coat.
Flake in the tuna in large chunks and fold gently so it stays in pieces.
Serve over the arugula. For meal prep, store the salad and arugula separately for up to 3 days and combine just before eating.

title: Lemon Caper Tuna Spaghetti
summary: A fast pantry pasta: canned tuna, garlic, capers and chili tossed with spaghetti, lemon and plenty of parsley.

ingredients.name: Breadcrumbs
ingredients.note: toasted in a little oil, for topping

instructions: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti 1 minute short of the package time. Save 1 cup of the pasta water before draining.
Meanwhile, warm the olive oil and garlic in a large skillet over medium-low heat for 2 to 3 minutes until the garlic is fragrant and barely golden.
Add the capers, red pepper flakes and cherry tomatoes if using; cook 2 minutes until the tomatoes start to soften.
Add the drained spaghetti, the tuna, lemon zest and 1/2 cup pasta water. Toss over medium heat for 1 to 2 minutes until the pasta is coated and glossy, adding more water if it looks dry.
Off the heat, stir in the lemon juice and parsley, then season with salt and pepper. Top with toasted breadcrumbs for crunch if you like.

title: Herb-Crumb Baked Cod
summary: Thick cod fillets baked under a buttery lemon, garlic and parsley crumb until the crust is crisp and the fish just flakes.
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F and lightly grease a baking dish or line a sheet pan with parchment.
Pat the cod dry, arrange in the dish and season with salt and pepper. Brush a thin layer of mayonnaise over the tops so the crumbs stick.
Mix the panko, melted butter, Parmesan, garlic, lemon zest, parsley and paprika until the crumbs look like damp sand.
Press the crumbs evenly over the fillets.
Bake 12 to 15 minutes, depending on thickness, until the fish is opaque, flakes easily with a fork and reads 145°F. If the crumbs need more color, broil for 1 minute, watching closely.
Serve with lemon wedges.

title: Cod with Tomatoes, Olives and Capers
summary: Cod gently poached in a garlicky tomato, olive and caper sauce in one skillet; great with rice, potatoes or bread.
instructions: Heat the oil in a large, deep skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and red pepper flakes for 1 minute.
Add the cherry tomatoes and cook 3 minutes until they begin to collapse. Stir in the canned tomatoes, olives, capers and oregano, and simmer 5 minutes to thicken slightly.
Season the cod with salt and pepper and nestle the pieces into the sauce, spooning some over the top.
Cover and simmer gently 8 to 10 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily (145°F).
Taste the sauce for salt, scatter with basil and serve spooned over the fish.

title: Goan-Style Coconut Fish Curry
summary: Firm white fish simmered in a tangy, gently spiced coconut and tomato gravy brightened with tamarind and fresh cilantro.

ingredients.name: White Fish
ingredients.note: cod, halibut or tilapia, cut into 2-inch chunks

ingredients.name: Kashmiri Chili Powder
ingredients.note: or 1 tsp paprika plus a pinch of cayenne

instructions: Toss the fish with 1/4 tsp turmeric and 1/2 tsp salt and set aside.
Heat the coconut oil in a wide pot over medium heat. Cook the onion 6 to 8 minutes until golden, then add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Stir in the coriander, cumin, chili powder and remaining turmeric for 30 seconds, then add the tomatoes and cook 5 minutes until they break down into a paste.
Pour in the coconut milk and tamarind paste plus 1/4 cup water. Simmer 5 minutes and season with the remaining salt.
Slide in the fish in a single layer, spoon sauce over it and simmer gently, uncovered, 6 to 8 minutes without stirring hard, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily.
Scatter with cilantro and serve with basmati rice.

title: Chili-Lime Tilapia with Corn Salsa
summary: Mild tilapia gets a chili-lime rub and a quick sheet-pan roast, topped with a fresh corn, tomato and avocado salsa.
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F and line a sheet pan with parchment.
Pat the tilapia dry and set on the pan. Mix 1 tbsp oil, the chili powder, cumin, garlic powder, lime zest and 3/4 tsp salt, and rub over the fillets.
Roast 10 to 12 minutes, until the fish is opaque and flakes easily with a fork (145°F).
While it bakes, toss the corn, tomatoes, avocado, red onion, cilantro and jalapeno with the lime juice, the remaining 1 tbsp oil and a pinch of salt.
Serve each fillet with a generous spoonful of corn salsa.

title: Mussels in Smoky Tomato and Garlic Broth
summary: Mussels steamed open in a smoked-paprika tomato broth with white wine and garlic; a quick, impressive pot for sharing.
instructions: Rinse the mussels in cold water. Discard any with cracked shells or any that stay open after a firm tap.
Heat the oil in a large pot with a lid over medium heat. Cook the shallots 3 minutes until soft, then add the garlic, paprika and red pepper flakes for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble 2 minutes, then add the crushed tomatoes and bring to a lively simmer.
Add the mussels, cover tightly and steam 5 to 7 minutes, shaking the pot once or twice, until the shells open wide.
Discard any mussels that stay closed. Stir in the parsley and spoon the mussels and broth into wide bowls with lemon wedges and bread for dipping.

title: Seared Scallops with Lemon Butter and Spinach
summary: Golden, sweet sea scallops seared in a hot pan and finished with a lemon-garlic butter over quickly wilted spinach.
instructions: Pat the scallops very dry with paper towels and let them sit 5 minutes, then pat again. Season both sides with salt and pepper.
Melt 1 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium heat. Add the garlic and spinach with a pinch of salt and toss 1 to 2 minutes until just wilted. Divide between plates and wipe out the pan.
Heat the oil in the skillet over high heat until it shimmers. Add the scallops, flat side down and spaced apart, and leave them alone 2 minutes until a deep golden crust forms.
Flip and add the remaining 2 tbsp butter. Cook 1 to 2 minutes more, spooning the butter over, until the scallops are opaque at the edges and just barely translucent in the very center.
Move the scallops onto the spinach. Stir the lemon zest and juice into the pan butter, spoon it over the scallops and finish with parsley.

title: New England Fish Chowder
summary: A thick, comforting cod chowder with potatoes, onion and celery, thickened with potato instead of flour.
instructions: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Cook the onion and celery 6 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes, clam juice, water, thyme and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then simmer, partly covered, 15 minutes until the potatoes are very tender.
Fish out the thyme stems and bay leaf. Mash about a quarter of the potatoes against the side of the pot to thicken the broth.
Stir in the milk and cream and bring back to a bare simmer over medium-low heat; do not boil or the dairy may separate.
Add the cod and cook gently 5 to 7 minutes, stirring only once or twice, until the fish is opaque and breaks into large flakes.
Season well with salt and pepper and serve topped with dill.

title: Tandoori-Spiced Salmon with Cucumber Raita
summary: Salmon marinated in spiced yogurt, roasted hot until charred at the edges, then served with a cool cucumber-mint raita.
instructions: Stir 1/2 cup yogurt with half the lemon juice, the garlic, ginger, garam masala, paprika, cumin, cayenne and 3/4 tsp salt.
Pat the salmon dry, coat the flesh side with the spiced yogurt and let it sit 10 minutes (or up to 1 hour in the fridge).
Heat the oven to 450°F. Line a sheet pan with foil, brush with the oil and set the salmon on it skin-side down.
Roast 10 to 12 minutes until the fish flakes easily and reads 145°F. Broil 1 to 2 minutes at the end for charred edges.
Meanwhile, mix the remaining 1/2 cup yogurt with the cucumber, mint, remaining lemon juice and 1/4 tsp salt.
Serve the salmon with the raita and rice or warm flatbread.

title: Chana Masala with Spinach
summary: Chickpeas simmered in a gingery, garam masala-spiced tomato gravy, with a big handful of spinach wilted in at the end.
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook, stirring often, until deep golden at the edges, 8 to 10 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, ginger and jalapeno and cook for 1 minute until fragrant. Add the cumin, garam masala, turmeric, paprika and cayenne and stir for 30 seconds so the spices bloom in the oil.
Pour in the tomatoes and cook, scraping the bottom, until they break down and the oil starts to separate around the edges, about 5 minutes.
Add the chickpeas, water and salt. Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, mashing a few chickpeas against the side of the pot to thicken the gravy.
Stir in the spinach a handful at a time until wilted. Finish with lemon juice, taste for salt, and scatter with cilantro. Serve over rice.

title: Red Lentil Dal with Spinach
summary: Silky red lentils cooked with turmeric, then finished with a sizzling cumin, garlic and tomato tadka and fresh spinach.

ingredients.name: red lentils
ingredients.note: rinsed until the water runs clear

instructions: Combine the lentils, water, turmeric and salt in a medium pot. Bring to a boil, skim off any foam, then simmer partly covered, stirring now and then, until the lentils collapse into a thick porridge, 18 to 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat the coconut oil in a skillet over medium-high heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 20 seconds until they darken slightly.
Add the onion and cook until soft and golden, about 6 minutes. Stir in the garlic, ginger and red pepper flakes and cook 1 minute more.
Add the tomatoes and garam masala and cook until the tomatoes slump into a jammy sauce, 3 to 4 minutes.
Scrape the tomato mixture into the lentils, add the spinach and stir until it wilts. Loosen with a splash of water if needed, then season with lime juice and salt. Top with cilantro.

title: Palak Paneer
summary: Golden seared paneer cubes folded into a bright, garlicky spinach sauce with warm spices and a splash of cream.
instructions: Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Blanch the spinach for 1 minute until bright green, then drain and plunge into ice water. Squeeze lightly and blend with 1/4 cup water into a smooth puree.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the paneer in a single layer until golden on two sides, 2 to 3 minutes per side, then transfer to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium and add the butter and onion. Cook until soft and lightly browned, 6 to 8 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger and serrano for 1 minute.
Stir in the tomato, cumin, garam masala and turmeric and cook until the tomato breaks down and the mixture looks glossy, about 4 minutes.
Add the spinach puree and salt and simmer gently for 5 minutes; don't boil hard or the color will dull. Stir in the cream, return the paneer and heat through for 2 minutes.
Finish with lemon juice, taste for salt, and serve with rice or warm flatbread.

title: Sheet-Pan Paneer Tikka with Peppers
summary: Yogurt-marinated paneer, peppers, onion and cauliflower roasted hot until charred at the edges, all on one pan.

ingredients.name: bell peppers
ingredients.note: red and green, cut into 1-inch pieces

instructions: Heat the oven to 450°F and line a large rimmed baking sheet with parchment.
In a large bowl, whisk the yogurt, lemon juice, garlic, ginger, garam masala, smoked paprika, cumin, turmeric, cayenne, salt and oil into a thick marinade.
Add the paneer, peppers, onion and cauliflower and toss until everything is well coated. Let sit for 10 minutes if you have time.
Spread in a single layer on the baking sheet, leaving space between pieces so they roast rather than steam.
Roast for 18 to 20 minutes, until the cauliflower is tender and the paneer is golden. Switch to broil for 2 to 3 minutes to char the edges, watching closely.
Scatter with cilantro and serve with rice, a squeeze of lemon, or wrapped in warm flatbread.

title: Anda Masala Egg Curry
summary: Hard-boiled eggs and sweet peas simmered in a deeply spiced onion-tomato masala; a thrifty, protein-packed weeknight curry.
instructions: Lower the eggs into a pot of boiling water and cook for 10 minutes. Transfer to ice water, then peel and cut a few shallow slits in each so they soak up the sauce.
While the eggs cook, heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the onions, stirring often, until deep golden, 8 to 10 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then the cumin, coriander, garam masala, turmeric and cayenne for 30 seconds.
Pour in the tomatoes, water and salt. Simmer until thick and the oil begins to pool at the edges, about 5 minutes.
Nestle in the eggs and peas, spoon the sauce over, and simmer 4 to 5 minutes until the peas are hot. Top with cilantro and serve with rice or flatbread.

title: Sweet Potato and Black Bean Tacos
summary: Smoky roasted sweet potato and black beans in charred corn tortillas with lime cabbage slaw and creamy avocado.
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Toss the sweet potatoes with the oil, chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika and 3/4 tsp of the salt on a rimmed baking sheet and spread out in one layer.
Roast for 15 minutes, flip, then add the black beans to the pan and roast 8 to 10 minutes more, until the sweet potatoes are tender and browned at the edges.
Meanwhile, toss the cabbage and red onion with the juice of 1 lime, the remaining salt and half the cilantro.
Char the tortillas one at a time directly over a gas flame or in a dry skillet over high heat, about 20 seconds per side, and stack them in a towel to stay warm.
Fill the tortillas with the sweet potato mixture, slaw and avocado. Finish with the remaining cilantro, lime wedges and salsa.

title: Mushroom and Pepper Fajitas
summary: Deeply browned mushrooms, peppers and onions tossed with lime and chili, piled into tortillas with black beans and avocado.
