instructions: Stir together the chili powder, cumin, smoked paprika and salt. Warm the black beans in a small pot with a splash of water and a pinch of the spice mix.

Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large cast-iron skillet over high heat until shimmering. Add the mushrooms in a single layer and leave them alone for 3 to 4 minutes until browned underneath, then stir and cook 2 minutes more.
Push the mushrooms aside, add the remaining oil, peppers and onion, and cook, tossing occasionally, until crisp-tender and charred in spots, 5 to 6 minutes.
Add the garlic and the rest of the spice mix and toss for 1 minute. Squeeze in half the lime and take the pan off the heat.
Warm the tortillas in a dry skillet. Serve the fajita vegetables with the beans, avocado, cilantro, salsa and the remaining lime cut into wedges.

title: Huevos Rancheros
summary: Crisp corn tortillas topped with cumin black beans, fried eggs and a quick blender ranchero sauce that simmers while you cook.
instructions: Blend the tomatoes, onion, jalapeno, garlic and salt until mostly smooth. Heat 1 tsp oil in a saucepan over medium heat, add the sauce (it will spatter) and simmer until slightly thickened, about 8 minutes.
Meanwhile, warm the black beans with the cumin and 2 tbsp water in a small pot, mashing about half of them with a fork.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the tortillas one or two at a time until blistered and just crisp, about 30 seconds per side. Drain on paper towels.
Lower the heat to medium, add the remaining oil and fry the eggs until the whites are set and the yolks are still runny, 2 to 3 minutes, working in batches.
Place 2 tortillas on each plate, spread with beans, top with 2 eggs and spoon over the ranchero sauce. Finish with avocado, cilantro and cotija.

title: Black Bean and Rice Stuffed Peppers
summary: Bell pepper halves packed with a smoky black bean, rice, corn and zucchini filling and baked under a blanket of melted cheese.
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Arrange the pepper halves cut side up in a 9x13-inch baking dish and bake for 10 minutes to soften.
Meanwhile, heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft, about 5 minutes, then add the garlic, zucchini, cumin and chili powder and cook 3 minutes more.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the rice, black beans, corn, salsa, salt and half the cheese.
Pack the filling into the peppers, mounding it generously. Pour 1/4 cup water into the dish and cover tightly with foil.
Bake for 20 minutes, then uncover, sprinkle with the remaining cheese and bake 8 to 10 minutes more until the peppers are tender and the cheese is bubbling.
Rest 5 minutes, then top with cilantro and a spoonful of sour cream.

title: Thai Red Curry with Tofu and Vegetables
summary: Golden tofu, broccoli and peppers simmered in a fragrant coconut red curry with a finish of lime and basil.

ingredients.name: red curry paste
ingredients.note: use a vegan brand; many contain shrimp paste

ingredients.name: basil
ingredients.note: Thai basil if you can find it

instructions: Heat 1 tbsp coconut oil in a large deep skillet over medium-high heat. Fry the tofu, turning occasionally, until golden on most sides, 7 to 8 minutes. Transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and the shallot and cook 1 minute. Stir in the curry paste and fry for 1 minute until it smells toasty.
Spoon in the thick cream from the top of the coconut milk and stir until it bubbles and turns glossy, then add the rest of the can, the broth, brown sugar and salt.
Add the broccoli and bell pepper and simmer 4 minutes, then add the zucchini and cook 2 to 3 minutes more until everything is crisp-tender.
Return the tofu, fold in the spinach until wilted, and take off the heat. Stir in the lime juice and basil, taste for salt, and serve over jasmine rice.

title: Thai Basil Tofu
summary: A fiery pad kra pao-style stir-fry of crispy crumbled tofu, green beans, garlic and chilies, finished with a fistful of basil.
instructions: Crumble the tofu with your fingers into rough pea-sized pieces. Pound or finely chop the garlic and chilies together into a coarse paste. Stir the soy sauces, sugar and water together in a small bowl.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat. Add the tofu and cook, stirring only every minute or so, until golden and crisp in places, 7 to 8 minutes. Scrape to one side.
Add the remaining oil, the garlic-chili paste and shallots and stir-fry for 30 seconds without letting the garlic burn.
Add the green beans and stir-fry 2 to 3 minutes until bright and crisp-tender, then toss everything together with the sauce until the tofu is glazed.
Turn off the heat, fold in the basil until just wilted, and serve right away over rice.

title: Thai Peanut Tofu Crunch Salad
summary: A hearty chopped salad of cabbage, crunchy vegetables, edamame and crisp tofu tossed in a tangy lime-peanut dressing.

ingredients.name: extra-firm tofu
ingredients.note: pressed and cut into small cubes

instructions: Toss the tofu with the cornstarch and a pinch of salt. Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and cook the tofu, turning, until crisp and golden on all sides, 8 to 10 minutes. Cool on a plate.
Whisk the peanut butter, tamari, lime juice, maple syrup, ginger, garlic and sriracha with 2 to 4 tbsp warm water until smooth and pourable.
In a large bowl combine both cabbages, the carrots, bell pepper, cucumber, edamame and most of the cilantro.
Pour over about two-thirds of the dressing and toss well; the cabbage holds up, so it can sit for a while without wilting.
Top with the crispy tofu, peanuts and remaining cilantro and drizzle with the rest of the dressing. For meal prep, keep the tofu and dressing separate until serving.

title: Mushroom Mapo Tofu
summary: Silky tofu and finely chopped shiitakes in a glossy, numbing-hot Sichuan chili bean sauce; ready faster than rice cooks.
instructions: Bring a pot of lightly salted water to a gentle simmer, slide in the tofu and let it sit for 2 minutes to firm up. Drain carefully.
Heat the oil in a wok or deep skillet over medium-high heat. Add the mushrooms and cook, stirring, until they release their liquid and turn brown and a little crisp, 5 to 6 minutes.
Lower the heat to medium, add the chili bean paste and red pepper flakes and fry for 1 minute until the oil turns red. Add the garlic, ginger and half the Sichuan pepper for 30 seconds.
Stir in the broth, soy sauce and sugar and bring to a simmer. Gently slide in the tofu and nudge it around with the back of a spatula so it doesn't break.
Simmer 3 minutes, then stir the cornstarch slurry and drizzle it in, pushing gently until the sauce thickens and clings, about 30 seconds.
Sprinkle with the green onions and remaining Sichuan pepper and serve over rice.

title: Kung Pao Cauliflower
summary: Crispy pan-fried cauliflower and peanuts glazed in a sweet, tangy, tingly sauce with dried chilies and Sichuan pepper.

ingredients.name: dried red chilies
ingredients.note: snipped in half, seeds shaken out

instructions: Whisk the soy sauce, rice vinegar, sugar, hoisin, sesame oil, 1 tsp of the cornstarch and 1/4 cup water in a small bowl.
Toss the cauliflower with the remaining cornstarch and the salt. Heat the oil in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat and spread the cauliflower in one layer.
Cook, turning every few minutes, until the florets are browned and crisp outside and just tender inside, 10 to 12 minutes.
Lower the heat to medium, push the cauliflower aside and add the chilies and Sichuan peppercorns to the oil for 30 seconds until the chilies darken but don't blacken.
Add the garlic, ginger, bell pepper, edamame and green onions and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Stir the sauce and pour it in, tossing until it thickens and glazes everything, about 1 minute. Toss with the peanuts and serve over rice.

title: Cabbage and Mushroom Egg Fried Rice
summary: A clean-out-the-fridge fried rice with browned mushrooms, sweet cabbage, peas and plenty of fluffy egg.

ingredients.name: eggs
ingredients.note: beaten with a pinch of salt

instructions: Break up any clumps in the cold rice with your hands so the grains are separate.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok or large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat. Pour in the eggs and scramble into large soft curds, about 1 minute. Transfer to a plate.

Add another 1 tbsp oil and the mushrooms and cook undisturbed for 3 minutes until browned, then add the cabbage and carrot and stir-fry until the cabbage is wilted and a little charred, 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the remaining oil, garlic, ginger and green onion whites for 30 seconds, then add the rice and peas. Spread the rice out and let it sit for 1 minute to toast, then toss; repeat twice.
Drizzle the soy sauce around the edge of the pan, add the white pepper and eggs, and toss until evenly colored and hot. Finish with sesame oil and green onion greens, with chili crisp on the side.

title: Miso-Glazed Eggplant Rice Bowls
summary: Roasted eggplant with a bubbling sweet-salty miso glaze, served over rice with edamame, cucumber and sesame.

ingredients.name: japanese eggplants
ingredients.note: or 2 small globe eggplants, halved lengthwise

instructions: Start the rice according to the package. Heat the oven to 425°F and line a baking sheet with foil.
Score the cut sides of the eggplants in a crosshatch pattern without cutting through the skin. Brush generously with oil and place cut side down on the sheet.
Roast for 18 to 20 minutes, until the flesh is completely soft when pressed.
Meanwhile, stir the miso, mirin, maple syrup, rice vinegar and ginger into a smooth glaze. Toss the cucumber with a splash of rice vinegar and a pinch of salt.
Turn the eggplants cut side up, spread the glaze over them and switch the oven to broil. Broil 3 to 4 minutes, watching closely, until the glaze bubbles and browns in spots.
Warm the edamame in the microwave or a pot of boiling water. Divide the rice among bowls and top with eggplant, edamame and cucumber, then sprinkle with green onions and sesame seeds.

title: Teriyaki Tofu and Broccoli Bowls
summary: Crispy tofu tossed in a quick homemade ginger-garlic teriyaki with tender broccoli over steamed rice; a reliable weeknight win.
instructions: Cook the rice according to the package. Whisk the soy sauce, mirin, brown sugar, garlic, ginger, 1 tsp cornstarch and 1/4 cup water to make the sauce.

Toss the tofu with the remaining cornstarch. Heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and cook the tofu, turning every couple of minutes, until crisp and golden, 8 to 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, steam the broccoli over boiling water, or microwave it covered with 2 tbsp water, until bright green and just tender, 3 to 4 minutes.
Lower the heat under the tofu to medium, stir the sauce and pour it in. Simmer, tossing, until it thickens into a glossy glaze, about 1 minute.
Divide the rice among bowls, top with the broccoli and teriyaki tofu, spoon over any extra sauce, and finish with green onions and sesame seeds.

title: Cabbage Okonomiyaki
summary: Savory Japanese cabbage pancakes studded with mushrooms and scallions, painted with a tangy sauce and a zigzag of mayo.

ingredients.name: green cabbage
ingredients.note: very finely shredded, about 1/2 small head

instructions: Whisk the flour, baking powder and salt, then whisk in the broth and eggs until smooth. Fold in the cabbage, mushrooms and most of the green onions; the batter should just coat the vegetables.
Stir together the ketchup, soy sauce, sugar and rice vinegar to make the sauce.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Scoop in half the batter and press into a round about 3/4 inch thick. Cover and cook until the underside is deep golden, 5 minutes.

Slide the pancake onto a plate, invert the pan over it and flip it back in. Cook covered 4 to 5 minutes more, until a knife in the center comes out without wet batter. Repeat with the remaining oil and batter.
Brush each pancake with the sauce, drizzle with mayonnaise, and sprinkle with the remaining green onions and nori. Cut into wedges to serve.

title: Tofu Bibimbap
summary: A colorful rice bowl of seasoned spinach, carrots, zucchini, mushrooms and sprouts with seared tofu, a fried egg and gochujang sauce.
instructions: Cook the rice. Stir the gochujang, rice vinegar, sugar, 1 tbsp sesame oil and 1 tbsp water into a sauce.
Blanch the bean sprouts in boiling salted water for 1 minute and scoop out, then blanch the spinach for 30 seconds. Squeeze the spinach dry. Season each with a little sesame oil, garlic and salt.

Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Stir-fry the carrots, zucchini and mushrooms one at a time, 2 to 3 minutes each, seasoning each with a splash of soy sauce and a bit of garlic. Set aside separately.
Add the remaining vegetable oil and sear the tofu slabs until golden, 3 minutes per side. Pour in the rest of the soy sauce and let it bubble and glaze the tofu.
Fry the eggs sunny side up until the whites are set and the edges are crisp.
Fill bowls with rice, arrange the vegetables and tofu around the top, and set an egg in the middle. Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve with the gochujang sauce to mix in.

title: Kimchi Tofu Stew
summary: A bubbling, spicy-sour kimchi jjigae made with vegetable broth, mushrooms, zucchini and soft tofu; comfort in 30 minutes.

ingredients.name: vegan kimchi
ingredients.note: chopped, plus 1/4 cup of its juice; many kimchis contain fish sauce

instructions: Heat the sesame oil in a medium pot over medium-high heat. Add the kimchi and onion and cook, stirring, until the kimchi softens and starts to caramelize, 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, gochugaru, gochujang and sugar and cook 1 minute.
Pour in the broth, kimchi juice and soy sauce and bring to a boil. Add the mushrooms, lower to a lively simmer and cook 8 minutes so the broth takes on the kimchi's flavor.
Add the zucchini and gently slide in the tofu. Simmer 4 to 5 minutes until the zucchini is tender and the tofu is hot through.
Taste; add a splash more kimchi juice for tang or soy sauce for salt. Top with green onions and serve bubbling hot with rice.

title: Gochujang Tempeh and Broccoli Stir-Fry
summary: Seared tempeh strips and broccoli tossed in a sticky, spicy-sweet gochujang glaze; big on protein and ready in 25 minutes.

ingredients.name: tempeh
ingredients.note: two 8-oz packages, cut into thin strips

instructions: Whisk the gochujang, soy sauce, maple syrup, rice vinegar, sesame oil and 1/4 cup water in a small bowl.
Heat 2 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the tempeh in one layer and sear until golden brown, 3 minutes per side. Transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil, broccoli and 2 tbsp water. Cover and cook 2 minutes to steam, then uncover and add the bell pepper and onion. Stir-fry until crisp-tender, 3 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger for 30 seconds, then return the tempeh and pour in the sauce.
Toss until the sauce reduces to a sticky glaze, 1 to 2 minutes. Top with sesame seeds and green onions and serve over rice.

title: Chickpea and Spinach Shakshuka
summary: Eggs gently poached in a smoky pepper and tomato sauce made heartier with chickpeas and a pile of spinach.
instructions: Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet with a lid over medium heat. Cook the onion and bell pepper until soft and sweet, 7 to 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, cumin, smoked paprika and red pepper flakes and cook 1 minute. Stir in the tomato paste and cook until it darkens slightly, 1 minute more.
Add the crushed tomatoes, chickpeas and salt and simmer, stirring occasionally, until thickened, about 8 minutes. Stir in the spinach until wilted.
Make 6 wells in the sauce with the back of a spoon and crack an egg into each. Season the eggs with a pinch of salt.
Cover and cook over medium-low heat until the whites are just set but the yolks still wobble, 5 to 7 minutes.
Scatter with feta and parsley and serve straight from the pan, with warm bread or rice for scooping if you like.

title: Mujadara with Crispy Onions
summary: Lentils and rice cooked with cumin and allspice, crowned with a tangle of crispy caramelized onions and a fresh tomato-cucumber salad.
instructions: Cover the lentils with plenty of water in a medium pot, bring to a boil and simmer 12 to 15 minutes, until just tender but not falling apart. Drain.

Meanwhile, heat 5 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the onions with a pinch of salt and cook, stirring often, until deep brown and crisp at the edges, 20 to 25 minutes. Lower the heat if they darken unevenly. Transfer half to a paper-towel-lined plate.
Add the rice, cumin, allspice and cinnamon to the onions left in the skillet and stir for 1 minute to toast. Add the drained lentils, 3 cups water and 1 tsp salt.
Bring to a boil, cover, and cook on low until the rice is tender and the water is absorbed, 18 to 20 minutes. Rest covered for 5 minutes, then fluff.
Toss the cucumber, tomatoes and parsley with the lemon juice, remaining oil and salt.
Pile the mujadara onto plates, top with the reserved crispy onions, and serve the salad alongside.

title: Sheet-Pan Za'atar Cauliflower and Chickpeas
summary: Cauliflower, crispy chickpeas, onion and blistered tomatoes roasted with za'atar, then tossed with kale and a lemony tahini drizzle.

ingredients.name: chickpeas
ingredients.note: 15 oz each, drained and patted dry

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. On a large rimmed baking sheet, toss the cauliflower, chickpeas and onion with the oil, za'atar, cumin and salt. Spread out in a single layer; use two pans if crowded.
Roast for 20 minutes, then stir, add the cherry tomatoes and roast 5 minutes more.
Scatter the kale over the pan, toss to coat it in the oil and roast 4 to 5 minutes, until the kale is wilted and crisp at the edges and the cauliflower is well browned.
Meanwhile, whisk the tahini, lemon juice, garlic and a pinch of salt. It will seize up; whisk in cold water a tablespoon at a time until smooth and drizzly.
Drizzle the tahini sauce over the pan, sprinkle with parsley, and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Lemony Halloumi Sheet-Pan Dinner
summary: Squeaky golden halloumi roasted with zucchini, peppers, chickpeas and cherry tomatoes, finished with lemon and fresh mint.

ingredients.name: halloumi
ingredients.note: sliced 1/2 inch thick; choose one made with vegetarian rennet if strict

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. On a large rimmed baking sheet, toss the zucchini, peppers, onion, tomatoes, chickpeas and garlic with 2 tbsp oil, the oregano, salt and pepper.
Roast for 18 to 20 minutes, until the vegetables are softened and starting to brown.
Nestle the halloumi slices among the vegetables and brush them with the remaining oil. Roast 10 minutes more, then broil for 2 to 3 minutes until the cheese is golden in spots.
Squeeze half the lemon over the pan, cut the rest into wedges, and scatter with mint. Serve immediately, while the halloumi is soft and warm.

title: Greek Chickpea Salad with Feta
summary: A no-cook chopped salad of chickpeas, crisp cucumber, tomatoes, olives and feta in a bright oregano vinaigrette.
instructions: Soak the sliced red onion in cold water for 5 minutes to tame its bite, then drain.
In a large bowl, whisk the olive oil, vinegar, lemon juice, oregano, garlic, salt and a few grinds of pepper.
Add the chickpeas and toss to coat; letting them sit in the dressing for a few minutes helps them absorb flavor.
Add the cucumber, tomatoes, bell pepper, onion, olives and parsley and toss gently.
Top with the feta and serve. It keeps well in the fridge for up to 3 days; add the feta just before serving if prepping ahead.

title: Zucchini Feta Fritters with Dill Yogurt
summary: Crisp-edged fritters of grated zucchini, feta and fresh herbs, served with a cool garlicky dill yogurt for dipping.
instructions: Toss the grated zucchini with 3/4 tsp salt in a colander and let it drain for 10 minutes. Then squeeze it hard in a clean towel until very dry; this is the key to crisp fritters.
Stir the yogurt, lemon juice, garlic, half the dill and the remaining salt together for the sauce.
In a bowl, beat the eggs, then mix in the zucchini, feta, green onions, remaining dill, mint and pepper. Sprinkle over the flour and baking powder and stir just until combined.
Heat half the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat. Drop in heaping 2-tablespoon mounds and flatten to about 1/2 inch. Fry until deep golden, 3 to 4 minutes per side.
Drain on paper towels and repeat with the remaining oil and batter, making about 12 fritters. Serve hot with the dill yogurt.

title: Zucchini, Spinach and Ricotta Frittata
summary: A tall, tender Italian-style frittata loaded with sautéed zucchini and spinach, dollops of ricotta and plenty of parmesan.
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. Whisk the eggs, milk, half the parmesan, salt and pepper in a bowl.
Heat the oil in a 10-inch oven-safe nonstick or cast-iron skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and zucchini until the zucchini is tender and lightly golden, 5 to 6 minutes.
Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the spinach, and stir until wilted and any liquid has cooked off.

Spread the vegetables evenly, pour in the eggs and cook without stirring until the edges begin to set, 2 to 3 minutes. Drop spoonfuls of ricotta and the tomatoes over the top and sprinkle with the remaining parmesan.
Bake 10 to 12 minutes, until puffed and the center is just set with only a slight jiggle.
Rest 5 minutes, loosen the edges, and slide onto a board. Top with basil and cut into wedges; it's good warm or at room temperature.

title: Tuscan White Bean and Kale Stew
summary: Creamy cannellini beans, kale and vegetables simmered with rosemary and tomato into a thick, rustic stew that tastes even better tomorrow.
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and celery with a pinch of salt and cook until soft, 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, red pepper flakes and rosemary sprig and cook 1 minute, then stir in the tomato paste and cook until brick red, 1 to 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, beans and broth. Bring to a simmer and cook 12 minutes. Mash about a cup of the beans against the side of the pot to thicken the stew.
Stir in the kale and simmer until tender, 5 to 7 minutes. Remove the rosemary stem.
Season with the salt, pepper and lemon juice, then ladle into bowls and finish with a drizzle of olive oil.

title: Misir Wot
summary: Ethiopian red lentils slow-simmered with berbere, garlic and ginger until thick, rich and warmly spiced.
instructions: Put the onions in a heavy pot over medium heat with no oil. Cook, stirring often, until they soften, dry out and start to stick, 6 to 8 minutes.
Add the oil and cook until the onions are soft and golden, 5 minutes more. Stir in the garlic and ginger for 1 minute.
Add the berbere and tomato paste and cook, stirring constantly, for 2 minutes until the paste darkens and the oil turns deep red.

Add the lentils, 4 cups water and salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered, stirring often and adding splashes of water if it gets too thick, until the lentils have broken down into a thick stew, 20 to 25 minutes.
Taste for salt and add lemon juice if you'd like brightness. Serve with rice or injera.

title: Moroccan Chickpea and Sweet Potato Tagine
summary: Sweet potatoes, chickpeas and zucchini stewed with cumin, cinnamon and dried apricots for a sweet-savory, warmly spiced one-pot meal.

ingredients.name: sweet potatoes
ingredients.note: medium, peeled and cut into 1-inch chunks

instructions: Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Cook the onion until soft and lightly golden, 6 to 7 minutes.
Add the garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then the cumin, coriander, cinnamon, turmeric, paprika and cayenne for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Add the sweet potatoes, tomatoes, chickpeas, broth, apricots and salt. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the zucchini and simmer uncovered for 10 to 12 minutes, until the sweet potatoes are tender when pierced and the sauce has thickened.
Stir in the lemon juice and taste for salt. Serve topped with cilantro and toasted almonds, over rice or quinoa if you like.

title: Mushroom Black Bean Burgers
summary: Hearty, smoky veggie burgers of black beans, browned mushrooms and walnuts that hold together and sear with a crisp crust.

ingredients.name: black beans
ingredients.note: 15 oz, drained, rinsed and patted very dry

instructions: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the mushrooms and onion, stirring occasionally, until all their liquid has evaporated and they're well browned, 8 to 10 minutes. Add the garlic, paprika and cumin for 1 minute, then the soy sauce. Let cool for a few minutes.
In a large bowl, mash the black beans with a potato masher or fork, leaving some beans in chunks.
Add the mushroom mixture, walnuts, panko, egg and salt and mix well. Chill for 10 minutes to firm up, then shape into 4 patties about 3/4 inch thick.

Wipe out the skillet and heat the remaining oil over medium heat. Cook the patties until a dark crust forms, 4 to 5 minutes, then flip carefully and cook 4 to 5 minutes more, until firm and hot through (160°F in the center).
Serve on toasted buns with lettuce, tomato, avocado and your favorite condiments.

title: Spaghetti Carbonara
summary: Silky egg-and-cheese sauce clinging to spaghetti with crisp bacon, made glossy with nothing but starchy pasta water.

ingredients.name: Bacon
ingredients.note: or pancetta or guanciale, cut into strips

ingredients.name: Eggs
ingredients.note: plus 1 extra yolk if you have it

instructions: Bring a large pot of well-salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until just al dente, about 1 minute less than the package says.
Meanwhile, cook the bacon (and smashed garlic, if using) in a large skillet over medium heat until the fat renders and the edges crisp, 6-8 minutes. Discard the garlic and turn off the heat.
In a bowl, whisk the eggs, Parmesan, and black pepper into a thick paste.
Scoop out 1 cup of pasta water, then drain the spaghetti and add it to the skillet with the bacon. Toss to coat in the fat and let it cool for about 1 minute so the eggs won't scramble.
Pour in the egg mixture with a splash of pasta water and toss constantly with tongs. Keep adding water a little at a time until the sauce turns creamy and coats every strand.
Serve right away with more Parmesan and pepper. If the sauce tightens as it sits, loosen it with another splash of hot water.

title: Pasta Puttanesca
summary: A punchy pantry pasta of tomatoes, olives, capers and anchovy that comes together while the water boils.
instructions: Start a large pot of salted water boiling for the pasta.

In a large skillet over medium heat, warm the olive oil with the garlic, anchovies, and red pepper flakes. Stir and mash until the anchovies melt into the oil and the garlic is pale gold, about 3 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, olives, and capers. Simmer briskly, stirring now and then, until the sauce thickens and the oil starts pooling at the edges, 12-15 minutes.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta until al dente. Reserve 1/2 cup of the cooking water, then drain.
Toss the pasta into the sauce with a splash of the reserved water until glossy. Taste for salt (the olives and capers are salty), fold in the parsley, and serve.

title: Pesto Pasta with Peas and Lemon
summary: Fresh basil pesto blitzed in minutes and tossed with pasta and sweet peas; a great home for a wilting bunch of basil.

ingredients.name: Baby Spinach
ingredients.note: or arugula, any wilting greens work

instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the pasta according to the package.

While it cooks, blend the basil, pine nuts, garlic, and Parmesan in a food processor until finely chopped. With the motor running, stream in the olive oil until smooth, then add the lemon zest, 1 tbsp lemon juice, and a pinch of salt.
Add the peas (and spinach, if using) to the pasta pot for the last 2 minutes of cooking.
Reserve 1/2 cup pasta water, then drain everything together.
Return the pasta to the pot, add the pesto and a splash of pasta water, and toss until creamy and evenly green. Adjust with more lemon juice or salt and serve with extra Parmesan.

title: One-Pot Lemon Garlic Pasta with Greens
summary: Pasta cooks right in its sauce with garlic, lemon and whatever greens need using, so there's only one pot to wash.

ingredients.name: Kale
ingredients.note: chopped, or spinach, chard or broccoli florets

instructions: Warm the olive oil in a wide pot or deep skillet over medium heat. Add the garlic (and red pepper flakes) and cook until fragrant and just golden, about 1 minute.
Pour in the broth, bring to a boil, and add the pasta. Cook at a lively simmer, stirring often so it doesn't stick, for 8 minutes.

Stir in the greens and keep simmering until the pasta is al dente and most of the liquid has been absorbed into a light sauce, 3-5 minutes more. Add a splash of water if it gets dry before the pasta is done.
Off the heat, stir in the butter, Parmesan, lemon zest, and 2 tbsp lemon juice until creamy.
Season with salt, pepper, and more lemon to taste, then serve at once.

title: Lasagna Soup
summary: All the flavor of lasagna in a cozy weeknight soup, with broken noodles, Italian sausage and a cool ricotta dollop on top.
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium-high heat. Add the sausage and cook, breaking it up, until browned with no pink left, 6-8 minutes.
Add the onion and cook until soft, 4-5 minutes, then stir in the garlic, tomato paste, and Italian seasoning for 1 minute until the paste darkens.
Add the crushed tomatoes and broth, bring to a boil, then add the broken noodles. Simmer, stirring occasionally, until tender, 10-12 minutes.
Stir in the spinach, if using, until wilted. Taste and season with salt and pepper.
Stir together the ricotta, mozzarella, and Parmesan. Ladle the soup into bowls, top each with a spoonful of the cheese mixture, and finish with basil.
Leftovers: the noodles keep absorbing broth, so thin the soup with extra broth or water when reheating.

title: Clean-Out-the-Fridge Fried Rice
summary: A flexible fried rice built on day-old rice and any stray vegetables, bound with scrambled egg and a quick soy-sesame sauce.

ingredients.name: Mixed Vegetables
ingredients.note: diced: carrots, peas, corn, peppers, broccoli, zucchini, anything

instructions: Break up any clumps in the cold rice with your fingers. Dice the vegetables into pea-size pieces so they cook quickly.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a large wok or skillet over high heat. Scramble the eggs until just set, about 1 minute, then move them to a plate.
Add another 1 tbsp oil. Stir-fry the onion, garlic, and firmer vegetables (carrots, broccoli) for 2-3 minutes, then add softer ones (peas, corn, peppers) for 1 minute.

Push everything to the side, add the last 1 tbsp oil, then the rice. Spread it out and let it sit for 1 minute to toast, then stir-fry until hot and slightly crisp, 3-4 minutes. Leftover diced tofu, chicken, ham or shrimp can go in now to heat through (meat or seafood makes it non-vegetarian).
Drizzle the soy sauce around the edge of the pan, add the eggs, sesame oil, pepper, and most of the green onions, and toss until evenly colored.
Taste, adding more soy sauce if needed, and top with the remaining green onions.

title: Kimchi Fried Rice with Bacon
summary: Sour, well-aged kimchi turns leftover rice into a savory, spicy skillet meal topped with a runny fried egg.

ingredients.name: Kimchi
ingredients.note: chopped, plus 3 tbsp of its juice; older and sourer is better

ingredients.name: Bacon
ingredients.note: chopped, or diced spam or leftover pork

instructions: Cook the bacon in a large skillet over medium heat until the fat renders and it starts to crisp, about 5 minutes.
Add the onion and kimchi and stir-fry until the kimchi softens and its edges caramelize, 4-5 minutes.

Stir in the gochujang, then add the rice, kimchi juice, and soy sauce. Turn the heat to medium-high and stir-fry until the rice is evenly red and a little crisp on the bottom, 4-5 minutes. Stir in the sesame oil and taste for salt.
In a separate nonstick pan, heat the vegetable oil over medium heat and fry the eggs until the whites are set but the yolks are still runny, 2-3 minutes.
Divide the rice among bowls, top each with an egg, and scatter with green onions and sesame seeds.

title: Pineapple Shrimp Fried Rice
summary: Sweet pineapple, juicy shrimp and cashews in a fish-sauce fried rice that tastes like Thai takeout from your own leftovers.

ingredients.name: Pineapple
ingredients.note: diced, fresh or canned and drained

instructions: Stir together the fish sauce, sugar, and curry powder (if using) in a small bowl.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat. Cook the shrimp until pink and just opaque, about 1 minute per side, then set aside.
Add 1 tbsp oil and scramble the eggs until just set; move them to the plate with the shrimp.
Add the remaining oil, then the shallot, garlic, and bell pepper. Stir-fry for 2 minutes, then add the pineapple and cook until its edges caramelize, 2 minutes more.
Add the rice and stir-fry, pressing it against the pan, until hot and lightly toasted, 3-4 minutes. Pour in the fish sauce mixture and toss.
Return the shrimp and eggs with the cashews and green onions and toss to combine. Serve with cilantro and lime wedges.

title: Garlic Sesame Noodles with Crisp Vegetables
summary: Chewy noodles in a glossy garlic-soy-sesame sauce, stir-fried with whatever crunchy vegetables are in the crisper drawer.

ingredients.name: Noodles
ingredients.note: lo mein, ramen, udon or spaghetti

ingredients.name: Bell Pepper
ingredients.note: sliced; or snap peas, cabbage, mushrooms

instructions: Cook the noodles according to the package, drain, and rinse briefly with warm water so they don't stick. Toss with 1 tsp of the sesame oil.
Whisk the soy sauce, remaining sesame oil, rice vinegar, brown sugar, and sriracha in a small bowl.

Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or large skillet over high heat. Stir-fry the broccoli and carrots for 3 minutes, then add the bell pepper and cook until crisp-tender and a little charred, 2 minutes more.
Lower the heat to medium, push the vegetables aside, and cook the garlic and ginger in the clearing until fragrant, 30 seconds.
Add the noodles and sauce and toss with tongs until everything is glossy and hot, 1-2 minutes. Top with green onions and sesame seeds.

title: Beef and Broccoli Lo Mein
summary: Tender slices of flank steak and broccoli tossed with springy noodles in a savory oyster-sauce glaze.
instructions: Toss the beef with the cornstarch and 1 tbsp soy sauce and let it sit while you prep.
Cook the noodles until just tender, drain, and rinse under warm water. Mix the remaining soy sauce, oyster sauce, brown sugar, sesame oil, and 2 tbsp water in a small bowl.

Heat 1 tbsp oil in a wok over high heat until shimmering. Sear the beef in a single layer without moving for 1 minute, then stir-fry until browned outside but still a little pink inside, 1 minute more. Transfer to a plate.
Add the remaining oil and the broccoli with 2 tbsp water. Cover and steam-fry until bright green and crisp-tender, about 3 minutes. Add the garlic, ginger, and green onions for 30 seconds.
Add the noodles, beef, and sauce and toss over high heat until the sauce coats everything and the beef is warmed through, 1-2 minutes. Serve hot.

title: Miso Butter Ramen Upgrade
summary: Turn a pack of instant noodles into a real meal with a rich miso-butter broth, jammy egg, corn and greens.

ingredients.name: Baby Spinach
ingredients.note: or bok choy or any tender greens

instructions: Lower the eggs into boiling water and cook for exactly 6 1/2 minutes for jammy yolks. Move them to a bowl of cold water, then peel.

In a pot, bring the broth and garlic to a simmer. Put the miso in a small bowl, whisk in a ladle of the hot broth until smooth, then stir it back into the pot along with the soy sauce. Keep below a boil so the miso stays fragrant.
Cook the noodles in a separate pot of boiling water for 1 minute less than the package says, adding the corn and greens for the last 30 seconds. Drain.
Divide the noodles, corn, and greens between two bowls and ladle the hot broth over them.
Top each bowl with half the butter so it melts into the broth, a halved egg, green onions, and a drizzle of chili oil and sesame seeds.

title: Spicy Peanut Rice Noodles with Tofu
summary: Crispy tofu and rice noodles tossed in a creamy lime-peanut sauce with crunchy raw vegetables for contrast.
instructions: Soak or cook the rice noodles according to the package, drain, and rinse with cold water.
Pat the tofu dry and toss with the cornstarch. Heat the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat and fry the tofu, turning occasionally, until golden and crisp on most sides, 10-12 minutes.
Whisk the peanut butter, tamari, lime juice, maple syrup, sriracha, and garlic with 3-4 tbsp hot water until pourable.
Toss the noodles with most of the sauce, the cabbage, cucumber, and carrots until evenly coated.
Top with the tofu, cilantro, and peanuts, and drizzle with the remaining sauce. Leftovers keep 3 days in the fridge; loosen the sauce with a little water or lime juice.

title: Japchae with Beef and Vegetables
summary: Chewy sweet potato glass noodles tossed with seared beef, spinach, mushrooms and carrot in a sweet sesame sauce.

ingredients.name: Tamari
ingredients.note: divided; use soy sauce if not gluten-free

instructions: Mix 4 tbsp tamari, the brown sugar, 2 tbsp sesame oil, and the garlic. Toss the beef with 2 tbsp of this sauce and set aside.
Boil the noodles until soft and chewy, 6-7 minutes. Drain, rinse with cold water, snip into shorter lengths with scissors, and toss with the remaining 1 tbsp sesame oil.
Wilt the spinach in the empty pot with a splash of water for 1 minute, squeeze dry, and season with the remaining 1 tbsp tamari.
Heat 1 tbsp vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook the onion, carrot, and mushrooms until tender, 4-5 minutes, then transfer to a large bowl.
Add the remaining oil and cook the beef until browned and no longer pink, 2-3 minutes. Add it to the bowl.

Add the noodles, spinach, green onions, and remaining sauce to the bowl and toss well with your hands or tongs. Taste, adding more tamari or sugar if needed, and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Use-It-Up Minestrone
summary: A hearty vegetable and bean soup that happily absorbs half-used vegetables, the last of the pasta box and a Parmesan rind.

ingredients.name: Zucchini
ingredients.note: diced, or green beans, potato, squash

instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots, and celery with a pinch of salt and cook until softened, 7-8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, zucchini, and Italian seasoning and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, broth, beans, and Parmesan rind. Bring to a boil, then simmer uncovered for 15 minutes so the flavors meld.
Add the pasta and kale and simmer until the pasta is tender, 8-10 minutes. Add a cup of water if the soup gets too thick.
Remove the rind, season well with salt and pepper, and serve with grated Parmesan and a drizzle of olive oil.
To freeze, cook the soup without the pasta and add freshly cooked pasta when reheating so it doesn't turn mushy.

title: Roasted Tomato and Red Pepper Soup
summary: Tomatoes, peppers and garlic roasted until jammy, then blended into a velvety soup; perfect for soft tomatoes past their prime.

ingredients.name: Tomatoes
ingredients.note: halved; any ripe or overripe kind

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Spread the tomatoes (cut side up), peppers, onion, and garlic on a rimmed baking sheet, drizzle with olive oil, and sprinkle with smoked paprika, salt, and pepper.
Roast until the tomatoes collapse and the pepper and onion edges are blackened in spots, 35-40 minutes.
Squeeze the garlic from its skins and transfer everything, including the pan juices, to a pot with the broth. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the basil and blend with an immersion blender (or carefully in batches in a blender, venting the lid) until very smooth.
Stir in the balsamic vinegar, taste for salt, and thin with more broth if you like. Serve with grilled cheese or crusty bread.

title: Potato Leek Soup
summary: A silky, gently oniony French soup of leeks and potatoes finished with a little cream; comfort in a bowl.

ingredients.name: Leeks
ingredients.note: white and light green parts, sliced and well rinsed

instructions: Swish the sliced leeks in a bowl of cold water to release any grit, then lift them out, leaving the dirt behind.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium-low heat. Add the leeks with a pinch of salt and cook, stirring, until very soft but not browned, 10 minutes. Add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the potatoes, broth, thyme, bay leaf, and salt. Bring to a boil, then simmer until the potatoes fall apart when pressed with a spoon, 20 minutes.
Remove the thyme stems and bay leaf. Blend until smooth with an immersion blender (or leave it a little chunky if you prefer).
Stir in the cream, season with pepper and more salt, and warm through without boiling. Top with chives.

title: Spanish Lentil Stew with Chorizo
summary: Smoky chorizo, paprika and brown lentils simmered with vegetables into a thick, filling Spanish-style stew.

ingredients.name: Chorizo
ingredients.note: Spanish-style cured, sliced into half moons

instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat and cook the chorizo until it releases its red oil and the edges crisp, 3-4 minutes.
Add the onion, carrots, and bell pepper and cook until softened, 7-8 minutes. Stir in the garlic, smoked paprika, cumin, and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the lentils, potato, broth, and bay leaf. Bring to a boil, then cover partially and simmer until the lentils are tender and the potato is soft, 30-35 minutes.
Mash a few pieces of potato against the side of the pot to thicken the stew. Remove the bay leaf.
Stir in the vinegar, taste for salt, and serve with crusty bread (not gluten-free) or over rice.

title: Weeknight Pho-Style Beef Noodle Soup
summary: A shortcut pho with a spiced, charred-aromatic broth poured over rice noodles and paper-thin raw beef that cooks in the bowl.

ingredients.name: Basil
ingredients.note: Thai basil if you can find it

instructions: Char the onion and ginger, cut sides down, in a dry pot over high heat until blackened in spots, 4-5 minutes.
Add the star anise, cinnamon, and cloves and toast for 30 seconds, then pour in the broth. Bring to a boil and simmer, covered, for 25 minutes. Strain, then season with the fish sauce and sugar.
Meanwhile, soak or cook the noodles according to the package and divide among 4 large bowls.
Lay the raw beef slices over the noodles in a single layer. Bring the broth back to a rolling boil and ladle it over the beef; the heat will cook it to medium-rare within a minute.
Serve with bean sprouts, basil, cilantro, lime wedges, jalapeno, and sriracha for everyone to add at the table.

title: Ginger Chicken Congee
summary: Soothing rice porridge simmered with ginger and chicken until creamy, topped with crisp shallots and scallions.

ingredients.name: Jasmine Rice
ingredients.note: uncooked, or 2 cups leftover cooked rice

instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs mostly clear. Combine it with the broth, water, ginger, and whole chicken thighs in a heavy pot and bring to a boil.

Reduce to a gentle simmer, partially cover, and cook, stirring every 10 minutes to stop sticking, until the rice breaks down into a creamy porridge, 50-60 minutes. (Leftover cooked rice needs only 20-25 minutes.)
After about 25 minutes, lift out the chicken (it should be cooked to 165°F), shred it, and set aside.
While the congee cooks, fry the shallots in the vegetable oil over medium heat, stirring, until evenly golden, 6-8 minutes. Drain on a paper towel; they will crisp as they cool.
Stir the chicken back in and season with fish sauce and white pepper. Add hot water if it's thicker than you like.
Serve topped with crispy shallots, green onions, a drizzle of sesame oil, and a halved egg or chili crisp if you like.

title: Tuscan White Bean and Kale Soup
summary: Creamy white beans, garlic and hearty kale in a rosemary-scented broth; a vegan pantry soup that tastes slow-cooked.
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots, and celery with a pinch of salt and cook until soft, 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, rosemary, and red pepper flakes and cook until fragrant, 1 minute.
Add the beans, tomatoes, and broth and bring to a simmer. Cook for 15 minutes, then mash about a cup of the beans against the side of the pot to thicken the broth.
Add the kale and simmer until tender, 5-7 minutes. Remove the rosemary stem.
Stir in the lemon juice, season with salt, and serve with a generous drizzle of olive oil.

title: Thai Red Curry Noodle Soup
summary: Coconut-rich red curry broth with chicken, rice noodles and vegetables, brightened with lime and fresh herbs.

ingredients.name: Red Curry Paste
ingredients.note: check the label for shrimp paste if that matters to you

instructions: Cook the rice noodles according to the package, rinse with cold water, and divide among bowls.
Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Fry the curry paste, garlic, and ginger, stirring, until very fragrant and darkened slightly, 1-2 minutes.
Stir in half the coconut milk and cook until it bubbles and the oil begins to separate, 2 minutes. Add the remaining coconut milk, the broth, fish sauce, and brown sugar and bring to a simmer.
Add the chicken, bell pepper, and mushrooms and simmer until the chicken is cooked through with no pink inside, 6-8 minutes.
Stir in the lime juice, then taste and balance with more fish sauce (salty), sugar (sweet), or lime (sour).
Ladle the soup over the noodles and top with cilantro and basil.

title: Blistered Garlic Green Beans
summary: Green beans seared until blistered and sweet, then tossed with plenty of garlic and a splash of soy.
instructions: Pat the green beans completely dry so they blister instead of steam.

Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Add the beans in a single layer and cook, tossing only every minute or so, until blistered and browned in spots and just tender, 6-8 minutes.
Lower the heat to medium, add the garlic and red pepper flakes, and stir for 30-60 seconds until fragrant but not browned.
Add the soy sauce and sugar, toss to coat, and finish with the sesame oil. Serve hot.

title: Sheet-Pan Roasted Vegetables
summary: A master method for roasting any mix of vegetables until caramelized and tender, the easiest way to rescue a crowded crisper.

ingredients.name: Mixed Vegetables
ingredients.note: bite-size: broccoli, cauliflower, carrots, peppers, zucchini, squash, brussels sprouts, onions

instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F with a rack in the upper-middle position.
Cut vegetables to similar sizes: dense ones like carrots and potatoes smaller, soft ones like zucchini and peppers larger, so they finish together.
Toss everything with the oil, garlic powder, seasoning, salt, and pepper, then spread across one or two rimmed baking sheets with space between pieces. Crowding makes them steam.
Roast for 15 minutes, flip with a spatula, and roast until browned at the edges and tender when pierced with a fork, 10-15 minutes more.
Squeeze lemon over the top and serve, or refrigerate for up to 4 days to add to grain bowls, pasta, or omelets.

title: Tangy Vinegar Cabbage Slaw
summary: A crunchy mayo-free slaw with apple cider vinegar and a touch of honey that stays crisp for days; great for half a cabbage.

ingredients.name: Honey
ingredients.note: or maple syrup to make it vegan

instructions: Toss the green and red cabbage with the salt in a large bowl and let sit for 10 minutes to soften slightly.
Meanwhile, whisk together the vinegar, olive oil, honey, mustard, celery seed, and pepper.
Add the carrots, green onions, and dressing to the cabbage and toss thoroughly.
Fold in the parsley and taste for salt and vinegar. Serve right away or chill; it keeps up to 4 days and tastes even better on day two.

title: Mexican Street Corn Salad
summary: Charred corn tossed with lime, chili, creamy dressing and salty cotija; all the flavor of elote with no cob to wrestle.

ingredients.name: Corn Kernels
ingredients.note: fresh, frozen and thawed, or canned and drained

instructions: Pat the corn dry. Heat the oil in a large cast-iron skillet over high heat, add the corn in an even layer, and leave it alone for 3 minutes until charred underneath. Stir and cook until well blistered, 4-5 minutes more. Let cool slightly.
In a large bowl, whisk the mayonnaise, sour cream, lime juice, garlic, and chili powder.
Add the warm corn, cotija, red onion, jalapeno, and cilantro and toss to coat.
Season with salt and more lime, sprinkle with chili powder, and serve warm or at room temperature.

title: Spinach & Feta Egg Bites
summary: Fluffy, grab-and-go egg bites that use up a bag of spinach before it wilts. Make a dozen on Sunday for the week.
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 12-cup muffin tin well with olive oil (or use silicone liners).
Blend the eggs, cottage cheese, salt and pepper until completely smooth and a little frothy, about 30 seconds.
Divide the spinach, tomatoes, green onions and feta among the cups, then pour the egg mixture over the top until each cup is about three-quarters full.
Bake 20 to 22 minutes, until the bites are puffed and the centers feel set when lightly pressed, with no wet egg showing.
Cool 5 minutes, then run a thin knife around each bite and lift out. They will deflate slightly; that's normal.
Refrigerate in a covered container up to 4 days. Reheat 30 to 45 seconds in the microwave.

title: Sausage, Egg & Potato Breakfast Burritos
summary: Hearty freezer-friendly burritos stuffed with crispy potatoes, sausage, soft eggs and cheddar. Wrap, freeze, and reheat on busy mornings.
instructions: Brown the sausage in a large skillet over medium-high heat, breaking it up, until no pink remains, 6 to 8 minutes. Transfer to a bowl, leaving the fat in the pan.

Add the olive oil and potatoes to the skillet with half the salt. Cover and cook 6 minutes, then uncover and cook, stirring occasionally, until tender and browned, 8 to 10 minutes more. Add to the sausage.
Whisk the eggs with milk, remaining salt and pepper. Lower the heat to medium-low and scramble in the same pan until just set but still glossy, 2 to 3 minutes.
Warm the tortillas in the microwave for 20 seconds so they fold without cracking.
Down the center of each tortilla layer potatoes and sausage, eggs, cheese, a spoonful of salsa and green onions. Fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
Eat right away, or cool, wrap each in foil and freeze up to 3 months. Reheat from frozen in foil at 375°F for 30 minutes, or unwrapped in the microwave 2 to 3 minutes, turning halfway.

title: Clean-Out-the-Fridge Frittata
summary: A flexible oven frittata for the odds and ends in your crisper drawer. Swap in any vegetables and cheese you need to use up.
instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F. Whisk the eggs, milk, salt and pepper in a bowl.
Heat the oil in a 10-inch oven-safe skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion, bell pepper and mushrooms until soft and any liquid has cooked off, 6 to 8 minutes.
Add the spinach and stir until just wilted, about 1 minute. Spread the vegetables evenly and scatter half the cheese over them.
Pour in the eggs and top with the remaining cheese. Cook without stirring until the edges begin to set, 2 to 3 minutes.
Transfer to the oven and bake 12 to 15 minutes, until puffed and the center jiggles only slightly when you shake the pan.
Rest 5 minutes, sprinkle with herbs and cut into wedges. Leftovers keep 4 days and are good cold in a lunch box.

title: Peanut Butter Banana Overnight Oats
summary: Stir together five minutes before bed and wake up to creamy oats. A soft, spotty banana makes them naturally sweet.
instructions: Mash the banana in a medium bowl with a fork until mostly smooth.
Stir in the peanut butter, milk, yogurt and maple syrup, if using, until combined.
Add the oats, chia seeds, cinnamon and salt and stir well, making sure no dry oats are stuck at the bottom.
Divide between two jars, cover and refrigerate at least 6 hours or overnight. They keep up to 3 days.
Stir before eating and loosen with a splash of milk if thick. Top with banana slices or a drizzle of peanut butter.

title: Rescue-Berry Smoothie Bowl
summary: A thick, spoonable smoothie bowl that turns soft berries and a handful of spinach into breakfast. Freeze fruit before it spoils to have it ready.
instructions: If your berries are fresh and soft, spread them on a tray and freeze for at least 1 hour first; frozen fruit is what makes the bowl thick.
Add the milk, yogurt and spinach to the blender first, then the frozen banana and berries.
Blend on low, stopping to scrape down and push the fruit toward the blades. Add milk only a tablespoon at a time until it moves; it should look like soft-serve.
Spoon into two bowls and top with granola, chia seeds and a drizzle of honey. Eat right away.

title: Yogurt Parfait with Quick Berry Compote
summary: Bruised or soft berries get a five-minute simmer into a jammy compote, layered with vanilla yogurt and crunchy granola.

ingredients.name: Strawberries
ingredients.note: hulled and chopped, or any soft berries

instructions: Combine the berries, maple syrup and lemon juice in a small saucepan over medium heat.
Simmer, mashing a few berries with a spoon, until saucy and slightly thickened, 4 to 5 minutes. Cool for a few minutes (or chill overnight).
Stir the vanilla into the yogurt.
In two glasses or jars, layer yogurt, compote and granola, then repeat. Finish with almonds.
For lunch boxes, pack the granola separately so it stays crunchy.

title: Brown Butter Banana Bread
summary: A tender, deeply flavored loaf for bananas that have gone brown and spotty. Browning the butter adds a toasty, nutty note.
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F. Grease a 9x5-inch loaf pan and line it with a strip of parchment.

Melt the butter in a small light-colored saucepan over medium heat, swirling, until it foams and smells nutty with golden-brown flecks on the bottom, 4 to 6 minutes. Pour into a large bowl and cool 10 minutes.
Mash the bananas into the butter, then whisk in the brown sugar, eggs and vanilla until smooth.
Sprinkle the flour, baking soda, salt and cinnamon over the top and fold with a spatula just until no dry streaks remain. Fold in the walnuts.
Scrape into the pan and bake 55 to 65 minutes, until a toothpick in the center comes out with a few moist crumbs. If the top browns too fast, tent with foil after 40 minutes.
Cool in the pan 15 minutes, then lift out and cool on a rack before slicing. Keeps 3 days wrapped at room temperature, or freeze slices.

title: Cheesy Black Bean Quesadillas
summary: Crisp, melty quesadillas ready in about 15 minutes, great warm or packed cold in a lunch box. Toss in wilting spinach if you have it.
instructions: In a bowl, lightly mash the black beans with the cumin, leaving some whole. Stir in the corn.
Spread the bean mixture over half of each tortilla, add spinach if using, and top with the cheese. Fold the tortillas in half.
Heat 1 teaspoon oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook two quesadillas at a time until golden and crisp on the bottom, 2 to 3 minutes.
Flip carefully and cook until the second side is golden and the cheese has melted, 1 to 2 minutes more. Repeat with remaining oil and quesadillas.
Rest 1 minute, cut into wedges and serve with salsa and sour cream. For lunch boxes, cool completely before packing.

title: Lunch-Box Snack Plate
summary: A no-cook, build-your-own snack box with protein, crunch and fruit. A smart way to use up the last of the veggies and cheese.
instructions: Peel and halve the hard-boiled eggs. Cut the carrots and cucumber into sticks and the cheese into cubes.
Core and slice the apple, then toss the slices with lemon juice so they don't brown.
Spoon the hummus into two small lidded containers for dipping.
Divide the eggs, vegetables, tomatoes, cheese, crackers, apple and almonds among the compartments of two lunch boxes, keeping crackers away from wet foods.
Pack with an ice pack and eat the same day.

title: Lemony Everyday Hummus
summary: Silky, bright hummus from one can of chickpeas in about 10 minutes. Ice-cold water is the trick to a whipped, fluffy texture.
instructions: Blend the tahini, lemon juice, garlic and salt in a food processor for 1 minute, until thick and pale.
With the machine running, add the ice water a tablespoon at a time; the tahini will seize and then turn creamy.
Add the chickpeas and cumin and process 2 to 3 minutes, scraping down once or twice, until very smooth. Add more water if it's stiff.
Taste and adjust with more salt or lemon. Spread in a shallow bowl, swirl a well with the back of a spoon, drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with paprika and parsley.
Refrigerate in a covered container up to 5 days.

title: No-Bake Oat Energy Bites
summary: Chewy peanut butter and chocolate bites that come together in one bowl. Keep a batch in the fridge for after-school snacks.
instructions: Stir the peanut butter, honey, vanilla and salt together in a medium bowl until smooth. If the peanut butter is stiff, microwave it for 15 seconds first.
Add the oats, chia seeds, chocolate chips and coconut and stir until everything is evenly coated.
Refrigerate the mixture 20 to 30 minutes so it's easier to shape.
Scoop by the tablespoon and roll into about 16 balls with slightly damp hands.
Store in a covered container in the fridge up to 1 week, or freeze up to 2 months.

title: Soft Fruit Crumble
summary: Turn berries, peaches, plums or apples that are past their prime into a bubbling, buttery-topped crumble.

ingredients.name: Mixed Berries
ingredients.note: or chopped soft peaches, plums or apples

instructions: Heat the oven to 375°F. Trim away any moldy or mushy spots from the fruit and cut larger pieces into bite-size chunks.
Toss the fruit with the sugar, cornstarch and lemon juice and spread in an 8x8-inch baking dish.
In a bowl, mix the flour, oats, brown sugar, cinnamon and salt. Rub in the cold butter with your fingertips until the mixture forms clumps.
Scatter the topping evenly over the fruit.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes, until the topping is golden and the fruit is bubbling thickly around the edges. Place a sheet pan underneath to catch drips.
Let rest 15 minutes so the juices thicken before serving, warm, with yogurt or ice cream.

title: Turkey Hummus Pinwheels
summary: Rolled-up tortilla spirals with turkey, cheese and crunchy vegetables that hold up well in a lunch box.
instructions: Lay the tortillas flat and spread hummus all the way to the edges; it acts as the glue.
Layer the cheese, turkey and spinach over each tortilla, leaving a 1-inch strip bare at the far edge. Place pepper strips across the end nearest you.
Roll up tightly from the pepper side, pressing the bare edge to seal.
Wrap each roll in plastic or beeswax wrap and chill at least 10 minutes (or overnight) to firm up.
Trim the ends and slice into 1-inch rounds with a serrated knife. Pack cold and eat within a day.

title: Weeknight Shakshuka
summary: Eggs gently poached in a smoky, spiced tomato and pepper sauce. Easy enough for a weekday breakfast or a quick dinner.
instructions: Heat the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium heat. Cook the onion and bell pepper until soft, 6 to 8 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, cumin, paprika and pepper flakes and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Add the tomatoes and salt and simmer, stirring now and then, until slightly thickened, 8 to 10 minutes.
Use a spoon to make 6 wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each. Cover and cook over medium-low 5 to 8 minutes, until the whites are set but the yolks still move.
Sprinkle with feta and cilantro and serve straight from the pan with something to scoop up the sauce.

title: Greek Orzo Lunch Salad
summary: A bright orzo salad with chickpeas, cucumber, olives and feta that gets better after a night in the fridge.
instructions: Cook the orzo in salted boiling water until al dente, 8 to 10 minutes. Drain, rinse under cold water and drain well.
In a large bowl, whisk the olive oil, vinegar, lemon juice, oregano, salt and pepper.
Add the orzo, chickpeas, cucumber, tomatoes, olives and red onion and toss to coat.
Fold in the feta and parsley. Taste and add more salt or lemon if needed.
Divide into containers and refrigerate up to 4 days. Stir before eating.

title: Frozen Yogurt Berry Bark
summary: Use up yogurt nearing its date by freezing it into a crackly, berry-studded bark. A cool snack or light dessert.
instructions: Line a rimmed baking sheet or a 9x13-inch pan with parchment paper.
Stir the yogurt, honey and vanilla together until smooth.
Spread the yogurt about 1/4 inch thick on the parchment. Scatter the berries, chocolate and almonds over the top and press them in gently.
Freeze until completely firm, at least 3 hours.
Break or cut into pieces and serve right away; it softens quickly. Store in a freezer bag up to 1 month.

title: Baked Feta Pasta
summary: Our take on the internet-famous baked feta pasta: a block of feta roasts with cherry tomatoes until jammy, then gets stirred into a creamy sauce.
instructions: Heat the oven to 400°F. In a 9x13-inch baking dish, toss the tomatoes and garlic with the olive oil, pepper flakes, salt and pepper.
Nestle the feta block in the center and turn it once to coat with oil.
Bake 30 to 35 minutes, until the tomatoes have burst and the feta is soft and golden at the edges.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta in salted boiling water until al dente. Reserve 1/2 cup pasta water, then drain.
Mash the feta and tomatoes together in the dish until creamy. Add the pasta and stir, loosening with pasta water a splash at a time until glossy.
Fold in the basil and lemon zest and serve right away.

title: Marry Me Chicken
summary: Our take on the internet-famous creamy chicken skillet with sun-dried tomatoes, garlic and parmesan. Rich, cozy and on the table in about 35 minutes.
instructions: Pat the chicken dry and season both sides with the salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Sear the chicken until golden, 4 to 5 minutes per side (it will finish in the sauce). Transfer to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium, add the butter, garlic, sun-dried tomatoes, Italian seasoning and pepper flakes, and cook 1 minute until fragrant.
Pour in the broth, scraping up the browned bits, then stir in the cream and parmesan. Simmer until slightly thickened, 3 to 4 minutes.
Return the chicken and its juices to the pan and simmer, spooning sauce over it, until it reaches 165°F in the thickest part, 4 to 6 minutes.
Scatter with basil and serve with pasta, rice or crusty bread to soak up the sauce.

title: Spicy Smashed Cucumber Salad
summary: Our take on the internet-famous smashed cucumber salad: craggy cucumbers soak up a garlicky soy, sesame and chili dressing in minutes.
instructions: Lay a cucumber on a cutting board and press or whack it with the flat side of a large knife or a rolling pin until it cracks open. Repeat along its length.
Tear or cut the cracked cucumbers into bite-size chunks, toss with the salt in a colander and let drain 10 minutes.
Meanwhile, whisk the garlic, soy sauce, vinegar, sesame oil, sugar and chili crisp in a serving bowl.
Shake off the liquid from the cucumbers (don't rinse) and toss them in the dressing.
Top with sesame seeds and green onion. Serve within an hour for the best crunch.

title: Leftover Salmon Rice Bowl
summary: Our take on the internet-famous salmon rice bowl: leftover salmon and day-old rice get mashed with spicy mayo and scooped up with crisp seaweed.
instructions: Flake the salmon over the rice in a microwave-safe bowl and sprinkle with a teaspoon of water.
Cover the bowl loosely (a damp paper towel or parchment works) and microwave 1 to 2 minutes, until steaming hot throughout.
Stir the mayonnaise and sriracha together. Drizzle the soy sauce and spicy mayo over the salmon and rice and mash everything together with a fork.
Top with avocado, cucumber, kimchi and sesame seeds.
Scoop bites of the rice mixture onto seaweed sheets and eat like little hand rolls.

title: Birria-Style Beef Tacos
summary: Our take on the internet-famous dipped, crispy beef tacos: chile-braised beef, melty cheese and a cup of rich broth for dunking.
instructions: Season the beef with the salt. Sear in batches in a large oiled Dutch oven over medium-high heat until browned on all sides, about 8 minutes per batch. Set aside.
Toast the chiles in a dry skillet 20 to 30 seconds per side until fragrant but not blackened. Soak in 2 cups of hot broth for 15 minutes.
Blend the chiles and their soaking broth with the onion, garlic, tomatoes, vinegar, cumin and oregano until very smooth.
Return the beef to the pot, strain the sauce over it, and add the remaining broth and bay leaves. Cover and simmer on low (or bake at 325°F) 3 to 3 1/2 hours, until the beef shreds easily.
Shred the beef with two forks. Skim the red fat from the top of the broth into a shallow bowl, and season the broth with salt to taste.
Dip a tortilla in the red fat, lay it on a hot skillet, and top half with cheese and beef. Fold and cook 2 to 3 minutes per side, until crisp and the cheese melts.
Serve with cups of the hot broth for dipping, plus cilantro, chopped onion and lime wedges.

title: Smash Burger Tacos
summary: Our take on the internet-famous smash burger tacos: thin beef patties seared right onto tortillas, with melty cheese and tangy burger sauce.
instructions: Stir together the mayonnaise, ketchup, mustard and pickle brine for the sauce.
Divide the beef into 8 loose 2-ounce balls. Place each on a tortilla and press firmly into a thin, even layer that reaches nearly to the edges. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat a large cast-iron skillet or griddle over medium-high heat. Place tacos meat-side down and cook until deeply browned, 3 to 4 minutes.
Flip so the tortilla is on the bottom, top the meat with a slice of cheese, and cook until the tortilla is crisp and the cheese melts, 1 to 2 minutes. The beef should have no pink remaining.
Fold each taco and fill with sauce, lettuce, pickles and onion. Serve hot.

title: Crispy Rice Salad
summary: Our take on the internet-famous crispy rice salad: day-old rice roasted until crunchy, tossed with herbs, peanuts and a zingy lime dressing.
instructions: Heat the oven to 425°F. Break up the cold rice with your hands and toss with the oil and 1 tablespoon soy sauce.
Spread the rice in a thin, packed layer on a parchment-lined sheet pan. Roast 12 minutes, then break into pieces, flip, and roast 10 to 13 minutes more until golden and crunchy.
Meanwhile, whisk the lime juice, remaining soy sauce, maple syrup, garlic and chile for the dressing.
In a large bowl, combine the edamame, cucumber, carrot, green onions and most of the herbs.
Add the crispy rice and dressing just before serving and toss. Top with peanuts and remaining herbs so everything stays crunchy.

title: Cottage Cheese Flatbread
summary: Our take on the internet-famous two-ingredient flatbread: blended cottage cheese and eggs bake into a bendy, high-protein wrap.
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper (not foil; it will stick).
Blend the cottage cheese, eggs, Italian seasoning, garlic powder and salt until completely smooth.
Pour onto the parchment and spread into a thin, even rectangle about 10 by 12 inches.
Bake 30 to 40 minutes, until golden all over with browned edges and dry to the touch in the center.
Cool 10 minutes so it firms up, then peel off the parchment. Fill with spinach, tomato or your favorite wrap fillings, roll up and slice.

title: Air-Fryer Pasta Chips with Whipped Feta
summary: Our take on the internet-famous pasta chips: boiled pasta air-fried until crunchy, with a tangy whipped feta dip.
instructions: Cook the pasta in salted boiling water for 2 minutes less than the package says. Drain well and pat very dry with a towel.
Toss the pasta with the olive oil, parmesan, Italian seasoning, garlic powder and salt.
Air-fry in a single layer at 400°F for 8 to 12 minutes, shaking every 3 minutes, until golden and crunchy. Work in batches. (Or bake at 425°F for 18 to 22 minutes, stirring halfway.)
Blend the feta, yogurt, lemon juice and honey until smooth and fluffy.
Let the chips cool 5 minutes; they crisp more as they cool. Serve with the dip.

title: Spicy Vodka Rigatoni
summary: Our take on the internet-famous spicy vodka pasta: a blushing, creamy tomato sauce with a gentle chili kick clinging to every tube.
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Warm the oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Cook the shallot and garlic until soft, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the tomato paste and pepper flakes and cook, stirring often, until the paste darkens to brick red and starts to stick, 3 to 5 minutes.
Pour in the vodka if using and scrape the pan until it has mostly cooked off, about 1 minute. Stir in the cream and salt and keep on low heat.
Cook the rigatoni until just al dente. Reserve 1 cup pasta water and drain.
Add the pasta, butter, parmesan and 1/2 cup pasta water to the sauce and toss over medium heat until glossy and clinging, adding more water if needed. Top with basil and more parmesan.

title: Feta Fried Eggs
summary: Our take on the internet-famous feta eggs: crumbled feta melts and crisps into a lacy crust under two jammy fried eggs.
instructions: Sprinkle the feta in a ring in a nonstick skillet and set over medium heat. Add the pepper flakes.
Cook until the feta melts and begins to bubble at the edges, 1 to 2 minutes.
Crack the eggs into the center of the ring. Cover and cook 3 to 4 minutes, until the whites are set, the yolks are still runny, and the feta underneath is golden and crisp.
Slide onto toast spread with avocado, if using, and finish with dill and a small drizzle of honey.

title: Crispy Smashed Potatoes
summary: Our take on the internet-famous smashed potatoes: tender boiled potatoes flattened and roasted until the edges shatter.
instructions: Cover the potatoes with cold water in a pot, add 1 teaspoon salt and bring to a boil. Simmer until a knife slides in easily, 15 to 20 minutes.
Drain and let the potatoes steam-dry in the colander 5 minutes. Heat the oven to 450°F.
Brush a sheet pan with half the oil. Place the potatoes on it, spaced apart, and press each with the bottom of a glass until about 1/2 inch thick.
Brush the tops with the remaining oil and sprinkle with the remaining salt, paprika and pepper.
Roast 25 to 30 minutes, until the edges are deep golden and crackly.
Toss the garlic over the potatoes for the last 5 minutes. Finish with parsley and a squeeze of lemon.

title: Dense Bean Salad
summary: Our take on the internet-famous dense bean salad: more beans than greens, lots of crunchy veg and herbs, and a punchy vinaigrette. Great for meal prep.
instructions: In a large bowl, whisk the olive oil, vinegar, lemon juice, mustard, garlic, oregano, salt and pepper.
Add the red onion and let it sit in the dressing 5 minutes to mellow.
Add the chickpeas, cannellini beans, cucumber, bell pepper and olives and toss well.
Fold in the parsley and basil; this is a great way to use herbs that are starting to wilt.
Taste and adjust salt and vinegar. Eat right away or refrigerate up to 4 days in covered containers.

title: Green Goddess Chopped Salad
summary: Our take on the internet-famous green goddess salad: finely chopped cabbage and cucumber in a creamy, herby dressing you scoop up like a dip.
instructions: Blend the basil, spinach, chives, cashews, olive oil, lemon juice, vinegar, garlic, water, salt and nutritional yeast until very smooth and bright green, 1 to 2 minutes.
Taste the dressing and adjust with more salt or lemon; it should be punchy.
Chop the cabbage, cucumbers and green onions very finely, about the size of peas, and combine in a large bowl.
Pour the dressing over the vegetables and toss thoroughly to coat.
Serve as a salad or scoop up with tortilla chips. Refrigerate up to 3 days; drain any liquid before eating.

title: Blender Baked Oats
summary: Our take on the internet-famous baked oats: an overripe banana, oats and an egg blend into a single-serve breakfast that bakes up like a soft cake.
instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F and grease a 10- to 12-ounce oven-safe ramekin or small baking dish.
Blend the oats, banana, egg, milk, maple syrup, baking powder, vanilla and salt until smooth, about 30 seconds.
Pour into the ramekin and scatter the blueberries or chocolate chips over the top.
Bake 22 to 26 minutes, until domed and golden and the center springs back when pressed.
Cool 5 minutes before eating; the middle stays soft and cake-like.

title: Whipped Coffee
summary: Our take on the internet-famous whipped coffee: instant coffee, sugar and hot water whisked into a fluffy cloud over cold milk.
instructions: Combine the instant coffee, sugar and hot water in a medium bowl. Regular ground coffee won't whip, so be sure to use instant.
Whisk vigorously by hand for 3 to 5 minutes, or 1 to 2 minutes with a hand mixer, until pale caramel colored and thick enough to hold soft peaks.
Fill two glasses with ice and pour in the milk.
Spoon the whipped coffee over the milk and stir it in as you drink.

title: Simple Chicken and Rice Soup
summary: Soft rice, tender shredded chicken and carrots in a mild broth. Plain, warm and easy to make when you're running low.
instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrots and celery and cook 6 to 8 minutes until soft but not browned.
Pour in the broth, add the whole chicken breasts and bring to a gentle simmer. Cook 15 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through.
Lift out the chicken and stir the rice into the pot. Simmer 15 to 18 minutes, until the rice is very tender.
Meanwhile, shred the chicken with two forks. Return it to the pot and season with salt and pepper.
Add a splash more broth or water if it's thick. Serve warm, with dill on top if you like.

title: Egg Drop Soup
summary: Silky ribbons of egg in a lightly thickened ginger broth. Ready in 15 minutes with things you probably have.
instructions: Bring the broth and ginger slices to a simmer in a saucepan and let them steep 5 minutes, then fish out the ginger.
Stir the cornstarch into the cold water until smooth. Stir it into the simmering broth and cook 1 minute, until slightly thickened.
Beat the eggs with the soy sauce. Stir the soup in one direction, then pour in the eggs in a thin stream so they set into soft ribbons.
Turn off the heat, taste for salt, and scatter with green onions and a few drops of sesame oil if you like.

title: Pastina in Brodo
summary: Tiny pasta in hot broth, stirred with egg and Parmesan until creamy. The small, warm bowl many Italian families make when someone's unwell.
instructions: Bring the broth to a boil in a small saucepan. Add the pasta and cook, stirring now and then, until tender, about 8 minutes.
Beat the egg with the Parmesan in a small bowl.
Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the egg mixture quickly so it turns creamy rather than scrambled, then stir in the butter.
Season with black pepper, add a squeeze of lemon if you like, and serve right away.

title: Soft Scrambled Eggs on Toast
summary: Eggs cooked low and slow until soft and creamy, on plain toast. Gentle, quick and made from staples.
instructions: Whisk the eggs, milk and salt until no streaks of white remain.
Melt the butter in a nonstick pan over low heat. Add the eggs and stir slowly with a spatula, pushing them from the edges to the middle.
Keep the heat low and take the pan off when the eggs are softly set but still look a little wet; they finish cooking on the plate.
Toast the bread and spoon the eggs on top. Add chives if you like.

title: Banana Cinnamon Porridge
summary: Creamy oats cooked with milk, sweetened with mashed banana and a little cinnamon. A soft, warm breakfast in 15 minutes.
instructions: Bring the milk, water and salt to a simmer in a small saucepan.
Stir in the oats and cinnamon and cook over low heat, stirring often, 5 to 6 minutes until thick and creamy.
Mash half the banana and stir it in; slice the rest for the top.
Spoon into bowls, top with the banana slices and a drizzle of honey if you like.

title: Tofu Miso Soup with Rice
summary: Soft tofu in a mild miso broth with a bowl of plain rice. Light, warm and ready in 25 minutes.
instructions: Rinse the rice, then simmer it covered with 3/4 cup of the water over low heat for 15 minutes. Let it stand 5 minutes.
Bring the remaining 3 cups of water to a gentle simmer in a saucepan. Cut the tofu into small cubes and warm it in the water for 2 minutes.
Turn off the heat. Whisk the miso with a ladle of the hot water until smooth, then stir it back in; don't let it boil again.
Spoon the rice into bowls, ladle the soup alongside, and scatter with green onions.

title: Simple Moong Dal Khichdi
summary: Rice and yellow lentils simmered soft with a little butter, cumin and turmeric. A mild, porridge-like one-pot meal many Indian families make for someone feeling poorly.

ingredients.name: Yellow lentils
ingredients.note: split moong dal; red lentils work too

instructions: Rinse the rice and lentils together in a sieve until the water runs mostly clear.
Melt the butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds, then stir in the ginger and turmeric.
Add the rice, lentils, water and salt. Bring to a boil, then cover and simmer on low 25 to 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and porridge-like.
Add a splash of hot water if you like it looser, and serve warm.

title: Carrot Ginger Soup
summary: Smooth carrot soup warmed with a little fresh ginger. Mild and bright, and it freezes well, so you can keep some ready for a rough day.
instructions: Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat. Add the onion and cook 5 minutes until soft.
Add the carrots and ginger and stir for a minute, then pour in the broth and salt.
Bring to a boil, cover and simmer 20 to 25 minutes, until the carrots are very tender.
Blend until smooth, in batches or with a stick blender, adding a little water if it's too thick. Serve with a spoonful of yogurt if you like.

title: Warm Cinnamon Applesauce
summary: Apples simmered soft with cinnamon and mashed. Gentle and lightly sweet; good warm in a bowl or cold from the fridge.
instructions: Peel, core and chop the apples into rough chunks.
Put them in a saucepan with the water, lemon juice and cinnamon. Cover and simmer over medium-low heat 15 to 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until very soft.
Mash with a potato masher or fork, smooth or chunky as you like, and stir in honey to taste.
Serve warm, or chill and keep in the fridge for up to a week.

title: Simple Mashed Potatoes
summary: Soft, buttery mashed potatoes with just milk, butter and salt. A plain, warm side that goes with almost anything.
instructions: Peel the potatoes, cut them into even chunks and put them in a pot of cold salted water.
Bring to a boil and simmer 15 to 20 minutes, until a knife slides in easily. Drain well and let them steam dry for a minute.
Warm the milk and butter together, then mash them into the potatoes until smooth.
Season with salt and pepper and serve warm.

title: Poached Chicken and Ginger Rice
summary: Tender poached chicken on rice cooked in the ginger broth, with cucumber and a splash of soy. Mild and warming, inspired by Hainanese chicken rice.
instructions: Put the chicken in a pot with the broth, the sliced ginger and the green onion whites. Add water to cover if needed and bring to a bare simmer.
Poach gently 15 to 18 minutes, until the chicken is just cooked through. Lift it out and keep the broth.
Heat the oil in a saucepan, stir in the garlic and grated ginger for 30 seconds, then add the rice, salt and 2 1/4 cups of the poaching broth.
Cover and cook on low for 15 minutes, then let it rest 5 minutes off the heat.
Slice the chicken and serve it on the rice with the cucumber, green onion tops, a little soy sauce, and a cup of the hot broth on the side.

title: Sopa de Fideo
summary: Thin noodles toasted golden, then simmered in a light tomato and chicken broth. A mild soup many Mexican families make on cold days or when someone's under the weather.

ingredients.name: Angel hair pasta
ingredients.note: or fideo, broken into short pieces

instructions: Heat the oil in a large pot over medium heat. Add the broken noodles and stir constantly 3 to 4 minutes, until golden.
Add the onion and garlic and stir 1 minute, then pour in the tomato sauce and let it bubble for a minute.
Add the broth and salt, bring to a boil, then simmer 8 to 10 minutes until the noodles are soft.
Serve warm with cilantro and a squeeze of lime if you like.
